en: On the delightful peak of Kailāsa, frequented by hosts of Gandharvas,
the goddess, daughter of the mountain, who was seated upon Hara’s chest, questioned him.
The Goddess said:
O God of gods, Mahādeva, cause of creation, maintenance, and destruction;
O Blue-throated One, Lord of the world, Sovereign, Śaṅkara, O Hara!
Salutations to you, O Lord of the World, my protector, O Lord of the immortals!
You who are solely devoted to the protection of those who have come for refuge, the wretched, and the afflicted. (3)
O support of all, O supportless one, O common support, O upholder of the earth;
O support of the knowers of the Vedas and sciences, O bearer of the Gaṅgā—salutations be to you!
This supreme tantra has indeed been heard— the essence of essences, higher than the highest—
by hearing which one quickly attains the stainless world of Śiva.
In the Kālītantra, in the Kubjikā[tantra], likewise in the Kālīvilāsaka, in the Ḍāmara, in the Yāmala, in the Kālīsarvasva, and in the Yonitantra; (6)
In the Sammohana, the Vikrama, and the Kulārṇava Tantra,
as well as in the Mātṛkābhedatantra and the Samayācāratantra.
In the Vīratantra, the Toḍala, as well as in the Bhairavatantra,
the Jñānatantra, and the Nirvāṇa, this was heard with the utmost reverence.
Now I desire to hear, O Lord, that which is more secret than the secret,
the essence of essences, the supreme purifier of all embodied beings; having heard it, the individual soul attains the state of Śiva— of this there is no doubt.
The illustrious Śiva said: "O Śaṅkarī, you are blessed; you are devoted to your husband; you are as dear to me as my own life.
Because women are by nature fickle-minded, O beloved, I did not speak [of this] to you before."
Now, knowing your steadfastness, O beloved, I shall speak to you:
there exists a certain *Muṇḍamālātantra*, the supreme means of accomplishment.
Having known this, the individual soul, having become Śiva, may roam upon the circle of the earth;
O Great Goddess, this captivating Tantra-rāja is to be kept most secret. 12.
"It has been told on every head by the Garland of Heads;
listen to this secret, O lady of excellent hips—what do you ask, O daughter of the mountain? (13)
Śrī Pārvatī said:
O God of gods, Mahādeva, Lord of the Universe, Maheśvara!
[Please explain] the conduct of these three and the purification of the disposition of these three.
The conduct of the three pledges, by which Durgā becomes pleased.
Śrī Śiva said:
As is Kālī, so is Tārā, and so is Tripurasundarī; likewise are Bhairavī, Vanadurgā, Chinnamastā, and Bagalāmukhī.
Dhūmā, Bhīmā, Annapūrṇā, Durgā, she whose essence is Kamalā, Mātaṅgī, Dhanadā, Parṇāvatī, and the bestower of the accomplishment of all goals. || 16 ||
O Maheśānī, O beautiful Śivā, various goddesses, great vidyās, and individual minor vidyās have been described separately in various tantras. (17)
The diverse conduct in difficult circumstances, whether right or otherwise, as well as the Muṇḍamālā Mahātantra, which is the means for attaining knowledge for all. (18)
O Maheśānī, Durgā is one and Sadāśiva is the one God;
I alone am the god Śiva, and there is no other god whatsoever. (19)
That Bhavānī shall indeed always bestow knowledge upon my wife;
at that very moment, perfection and unwavering devotion arise.
Without knowledge, I do not know the supreme reality on this earth;
therefore, one who is skilled in all things should cultivate supreme knowledge. (21)
Listen, O Goddess of gods, to the cause of my practice which is difficult to attain;
for beyond this, O Goddess, is the supreme practice that is most difficult to master. (22)
It brings about all peace, removes all suffering, causes the destruction of all diseases, and purifies all spiritual accomplishments. || 23 ||

That which is difficult to attain even for Brahmā and the others, and which is difficult for all to attain—Śiva—is he who, among the Śaktas on earth, possesses [this power]; of this there is no doubt.
By the mere knowledge of which one becomes liberated while living, the practitioner on the surface of the earth should recite the mantra with devotion, again and again. (25)
One who is liberated while living is eternally free and skilled in all actions;
he is one who shows the way to others and who desires both worldly enjoyment and liberation.
If he were to become wealthy merely by the wealth obtained in a dream, O Pārvatī, it would be like the delusion of silver arising in a mother-of-pearl shell. (27)
Likewise, he desires both worldly enjoyment and liberation from other philosophical systems;
without Durgā, I have no knowledge, and without Durgā, I have no delight. (28)
Without Durgā there is no liberation; I speak the truth, the absolute truth.
There is no devotion to the Three-eyed One that is stainless, nor any supreme ritual action more beloved than her.
Relying upon the two powers, he is the supreme worshiper of Śakti;
O Goddess, the first is very difficult to know, while the middle is adorned with five.
The rest is governed by one's own family; it does not exist, it does not exist, O fair-faced one!
I know the truth, I know what is beneficial, and I know it again, O fair-faced one. (31)
Without a thorough knowledge of Durgā, what learned man can cross over?
Who knows the supreme reality? Who knows the entire state? || 32 ||
Who knows the conduct of Bhairava? He who knows it is truly wise;
he is of noble lineage, he is a hero, and he is adorned with the fifth [initiation]. || 33 ||
O Mother of the World, O Sovereign of the World, O Victorious One! He who knows the true nature of Pārvatī while remaining impartial shall not take on a body again.
Having first worshipped the Guru and finally performing the supreme sādhana, the living being indeed becomes a partaker of all [attainments] through the power of action (kriyā-śakti). || 35 ||
O Mother of the World, there is no origin for Durgā; she belongs to me alone.
For others, however, there is indeed an origin in heaven or upon the surface of the earth. (36)
Therefore, truly, truly, and again truly, I say this:
those who are united with both existence and non-existence attain the stainless liberation.
O Śaṅkarī, as for the question you have asked, I know it all;
the supreme knowledge is known, O auspicious one with the formidable face. (38)
I shall now describe the conduct of this [goddess] and the conduct of her practitioner—conduct that is difficult to find in the world—among these very matters. (39)
The Guru alone is Śiva manifest; the Guru is the accomplisher of all aims.
The Guru indeed is the supreme reality; the entire universe is permeated by the Guru.
Without the grace of the Guru, what is the use of ten million rounds of purificatory rites?
O Goddess, without the worship of the Guru, nothing is accomplished on this earth. (41)
O Goddess, Bhairava himself takes away the splendors of the mantra of that person who performs the worship of the chosen deity without first performing the worship of the Guru. (42)
By contemplating with the intellect the oneness of the deity, the guru, and the mantra, the mantra will then become effective; otherwise, there is only failure.
Śrī Pārvatī said:
O Mahādeva, O Lord, how does the knowledge of oneness arise? [How do] the Guru in human form, the Mantra, and the Deity in the form of meditation [arise]?
And since mantras exist in the form of syllables, O Śiva, how can there be oneness? (44)
The illustrious Śiva said:
"O Pārvatī, you are blessed; you are equal to my very life; you are devoted to your husband, by virtue of your singular nature and your innate disposition from birth. (45)
But when these are joined with the state of being (bhāva-yoga), there is indeed only a single means;
for the mantra is born from the Guru, O beautiful one, and the Gurus are born from the mantra. (46)
Therefore, O Varārohā, the Grandfather [Brahmā] is the deity;
and by virtue of his contemplation, O Goddess, he is likewise the father of the father and the father of that father. (47)
From that [the teacher] arises satisfaction; in the opposite case, the reverse occurs.
The teacher is the creator, the teacher is the remover, and the teacher is the protector upon the earth. 48.
By the mere satisfaction of the Guru, all the deities become pleased;
when the Guru is satisfied, Śiva is satisfied, and when he is angry, the Three-eyed Lord is angry. (49)
When the Guru is pleased, Śivā is pleased; when he is angry, the beautiful goddess is angry.
Therefore, O Maheśānī, the Guru is the means for crossing the ocean of worldly existence.
The Guru is the creator, the protector, and the destroyer; he is the bestower of liberation.
The individual soul (jīva) is Śiva, and the divine Śiva is the soul itself—Śiva alone, both as the embodied soul and in his absolute state.
Bound by the fetters one is a living soul (jīva); freed from the fetters, one is Sadāśiva.
Having bowed at the lotus-feet of the Guru and meditated upon the Guru’s sandals, [one should proceed]. 52.
Having realized the supreme reality, he who indeed worships Kulacaṇḍikā is one who has achieved his purpose, he is blessed, he is grateful, and he is wise. (53)

O Great Goddess, one who knows the intrinsic nature [of this] becomes [enlightened]; of this there is no doubt—whether he meditates upon it, remembers it, worships it, or even bows down to it with effort. (54)
Whether through knowledge or even through ignorance, this time of worship bestows liberation upon that which is composed of consciousness,
non-dual, partless, and bodiless.
For the sake of the lay devotees' ritual purpose, there is the conceptualization of the form of Brahmā;
[he worships] the Goddess who consists of all the gods, the supreme one who consists of all the gods. (56)
For those who are ignorant, one should contemplate the Goddess, whose nature is the Supreme Brahman;
she is eternal, stainless, without support, and without refuge.
Sarvadhārā, Nirādhārā, Vijayā, and Jayāvahā;
as well as Saguṇā and Nirguṇā—thus Mahāmāyā is considered to be twofold.
When endowed with qualities through Māyā she is Sagunā, and when devoid of her she is Nirguṇā;
and when the Goddess is Sagunā, this Sadāśiva is likewise Saguna. (59)
O Great Illusion, you are devoid of qualities, and I am likewise devoid of qualities; of this there is no doubt.
You alone are the quality-less Power (Śakti), and I too am indeed quality-less.
O Goddess, he who worships the Saguna [Brahman] shall also, in no long time, become Nirguna;
for the Supreme Brahman transcends the qualities (guṇas), is devoid of desire, and is beyond all description.
That very [knowledge] is the supreme Vidyā, endowed with qualities such as Kālī;
it is for the benefit of the practitioner and for the grace of the Śākta.
The supreme Vidyā has arisen with its qualities; of this there is no doubt.
[Thus ends the first chapter in the Muṇḍamālā Tantra, in the dialogue between Pārvatī and Īśvara. || 1 ||
[Then the second chapter:
Once, the goddess Pārvatī, the auspicious one with a formidable face, asked the supreme Kālikā while smiling: "O Goddess Pārvatī," [she said]. 1.
Śrī Pārvatī said:
O Mahādeva, Maheśāna, Maheśvara, Sadāśiva! O highly fortunate one, I ask you a single question; please tell me, O Lord.
Without vyāna, kumbhaka, prāṇāyāma, and kulluka;
without japa, austerity, dhāraṇā, and the bridge (setu) itself. (3)
Without the *haṃsa*, without the *piṇḍa*, without the *bhāva*, and without the *pada*, how indeed can perfection (*siddhi*) arise? Tell me, O Lord, Teacher of the World! (4)
Śrī Śiva said: By means of the power of the Vāmarāśi [yantra], the recitation of mantras (japa) and worship must be performed by Brāhmaṇas, Kṣatriyas, Vaiśyas, and even by Śūdras and other castes.
O Goddess, those Śāktas who are Brāhmaṇas, O Caṇḍī, are remembered as Kṣatriya-Brāhmaṇas; the Vaiśyas and even all the Śūdras are Brāhmaṇas.
O Caṇḍī, Brāhmaṇas and Śaṅkaras should worship the Mother of the World, the beloved of Hara, with red flowers; she who is three-eyed and bears the moon upon her crest.
O Queen of the Gods, one should worship with devotion the Goddess Durgā, the sovereign of the three worlds and the bestower of liberation, using *vajrapuṣpa*.
Having taken a flower produced in the pleasure-chamber of a creeper that has not been touched by fire, one should offer it to Mahādevī.
O Goddess, there is the Svayambhukusuma, known as Raktacandana;
likewise, O fair-faced one, there is the Triśūlapuṣpa and the Vajrapuṣpa.
As an alternative, one may use red-sandalwood, which is dear to Hara;
for sometimes there may be liberation, and sometimes there is indeed worldly enjoyment.
For the practitioner of this [mantra], both enjoyment and liberation are held in the palm of the hand;
for if one is a yogi, he is not a seeker of pleasure, and if he is a seeker of pleasure, he is not a possessor of yoga.
The Kaula system consists of both yoga and enjoyment; therefore, one should practice the Kaula.
For there is no one who is merely a yogi, nor one who is merely an enjoyer, nor one who possesses yoga without [the other]. (13)

Whether he be a yogi or not a yogi, he will undoubtedly become an enjoyer of worldly pleasures— O Goddess, this is so for that person of deluded intellect who runs after [worldly things] without devotion to Śiva.
One would become neither a yogin nor an enjoyer even in hundreds of millions of kalpas;
yet by meditating on Rudra one becomes Rudra, and by meditating on Viṣṇu one becomes Viṣṇu.
By meditating upon Durgā, one certainly becomes Durgā; of this there is no doubt.
As is Śiva, so is Durgā; she who is Durgā is indeed Śiva himself. (16)
In this regard, that man who creates division is indeed one of deluded intellect;
O Goddess, he should contemplate the oneness of Viṣṇu, Śiva, and the others. (17)
The sinful man who creates division goes to the Raurava hell;
indeed, there is no worship equal to Durgā, and no fruit equal to Durgā.
There is no knowledge equal to Durgā, and no austerity equal to Durgā;
wherever the life-story of Durgā exists, there is the abode of Kailāsa.
This is the truth, this is the truth, this is the truth, O fair-faced one:
in heaven, on earth, and in the underworld, there is nothing dearer than Śakti.
O Dear One, [he should worship] those of the Saura, Gāṇapatya, and Vaiṣṇava sects, and likewise at the end, those of the Śākta sect, in due order, step by step.
Listen, O Goddess of noble form: there is no person superior to a Śākta.
Even Śaṅkara is himself a Śākta, directly partaking of the nature of the Supreme Brahman.
By whom Kālī, Tārā, Tripurasundarī, Ṣoḍaśī, Mātaṅgī, Chinnā, and Bagalāmukhī have been propitiated; (23)
O Great Goddess, that Śiva has been propitiated; of this there is no doubt. O Lady of Excellent Limbs, this supreme state of the Śāktas is to be kept most secret.
He who knows [this] in the midst of the earth is Śiva; there is no doubt about this.
He who constantly worships with joy the lotus-feet worshipped by Brahmā and the other gods—[he is Śiva]. (25)
Indeed, in a short time, he goes to the very temple of liberation;
for there is but one knowledge, one primordial nature (prakṛti), and one Śiva who is the Puruṣa. || 26 ||
"I alone proclaim that Vaiṣṇava-hood is indeed one and the same;
thus, whoever worships Durgā, the beloved of Hara, with such a mind," (27)
The practitioner should worship with yantra-flowers upon the mandala on the ground;
having thus performed the "crow's robe" (kākakañcu) breath control which bestows purification. (28)

One should perform the retention of breath (kumbhaka), the placement of the letters (mātṛkānyāsa), and the regulation of breath (prāṇāyāma) again and again; O auspicious lady, there are three types of breath regulation: inferior, superior, and middling.
From the lowest [level] sweat is produced; from the middling, the shaking of the limbs;
and from the highest, the abandonment of the earth occurs—of this there is no doubt. (30)
The vital airs are prāṇa, apāna, samāna, udāna, and vyāna;
and [the five subsidiary breaths are] nāga, kūrma, kṛkara, devadatta, and dhanañjaya. || 31 ||
Through breath control (prāṇāyāma), a profound rest arises for all;
[this is further enhanced] by hibiscus flowers, droṇa flowers, and beautiful karavīra flowers.
One should worship the supreme goddess Caṇḍikā with the utmost devotion using flowers of the black Aparājitā, Vajra, and Munipuṣpa.
One should bow with a spirit of devotion and worship Kālī, the beloved of Hara, who has a formidable face and is adorned with a garland of severed heads.
The creature appointed for the northern direction is adorned with all ornaments;
he is clothed in red garments and anointed with red garlands and unguents.
O Great Goddess, gradually contemplating "I am He" in this manner, the best of practitioners, having established himself as Durgā upon the seat of the Lord, [should proceed]. (36)
Having ascended a corpse in a cremation ground, the human practitioner situated in the center should recite the secret Great Mantra; he shall dwell in the abode of Kailāsa.
"I am Śiva and she is Śivā; this indeed is the constant meditation on the middle [state]. Having established oneself in the primordial state, one should joyfully meditate upon Kuṇḍalinī. (38)
At times, one should worship with ritual action according to one's capacity the goddess Tāriṇī, Durgā, the savior who delivers from distress, the delightful Brahma-vidyā.
One should meditate upon Mahādeva, the blue-throated Sadāśiva, the Lord of Gods who is hidden even from Brahmā and the others, accompanied by Śakti, within the thousand-spoked [lotus]. (40)
And this tantra, mantra, and yantra, which is difficult to find on the surface of the earth and is the speech of supreme nirvāṇa, [is not for] the hypocrite amidst the crowd of worldly beings.
O Pārvatī, O lady of excellent limbs, it must indeed be guarded like one's own womb;
O highly fortunate one, one should mutter the supreme mantra day and night.
By reciting this, one becomes a possessor of great knowledge and shall attain the state of a leader of the Gaṇas;
for I myself am Śiva-Brahman, I am Śiva, and indeed I am Bhairava. (43)
"I am Bhairava, I am Bhairava; Bhairavī is my beloved.
Having attained this knowledge through the mind, one becomes a supreme adept on earth. (44)
Having thus attained this supreme, eternal, changeless, and delightful knowledge, the living being may always roam upon the circle of the earth. 45.
One should worship the Supreme Goddess with water for the feet, the respectful offering (arghya), water for sipping (ācamanīya), and so forth;
he who does so should be known as eternally blissful and the accomplisher of all dharma and worldly goals. || 46 ||
O Caṇḍī, whoever bows down to Kālikā with devotion and ritual action, that living being attains the state of Śiva; this is the truth, the truth—there is no doubt. || 47 ||
Where is Yama? Where is Viṣṇu, the ascetic? Where is Kali, who harms through action?
One should always contemplate truth as the remedy for all mental affliction. (48)
Having adopted this procedure, the wise person should recite the mantra and meditate;
that person attains the state of Śiva in a very short time. || 49 ||
One should always perform ritual action; through such action one attains supreme perfection and constant purity. Therefore, one should never abandon it.
O fair-faced one, the accomplishment of the cremation ground and the mastery over corpses shall come about through the mere grace of Durgā; of this there is no doubt. (51)
The divine type is generally like a god, O Goddess; the heroic type has an uplifted mind; and likewise, the animal type exists on the surface of the earth, O Goddess, as well as the pure type.
Having heard this, that goddess Kālī, possessing a formidable lotus-like form and a portion of [Śiva’s] power, laughing, naked,
and with a divine body, spoke to the three-eyed Lord.
O Lord, that which was told as a secret has been heard by me with the utmost reverence;
yet I desire to hear once more that which is most secret and a profound mystery. (54)
O Lord, this divine [state] is difficult to attain; a hero who harms his own kind is not established even among animals—this was heard long ago in the Vīra-tantra.
Now I wish to hear the words of Brahmā concerning Sadāśiva.
The illustrious Śiva said:
"You have heard the Bhairava-tantra, the Yoni-tantra, the Kulārṇava,
the Kulācāra, as well as the Guptasādhana and the Gurutantra."
In the past, I heard the Nirvāṇa, the Samayācāra, and the Vīratantra; I also heard the Ḍāmara, the Ḍamara, the Ḍīna, and the Kālīvilāsaka. (57)
Seven crores of great texts have issued from my mouth:
the *Yāmala*, O Goddess, the *Brahmodya-yāmala*, and the *Viṣṇu-yāmala*. (58)
O Goddess, the Śivayāmala, the Mitrayāmala, and the Śaktiyāmala have been told and heard by you, O Durgā. (59)
Nevertheless, O Supreme Goddess, there remains a knot in your heart;
for in the past, the Tantra was well-expounded, and in the past, O Goddess, it was heard by you.
The convention, the conduct of the observance, the tantra, and likewise the symbolic convention;
that which is called the family convention is a convention of great extent. (61)
O auspicious one, the practice of the cremation ground and the practice of the corpse—these various and diverse states have been explained to you, O Goddess. (62)
But listen to one thing, O lady of beautiful limbs; I shall tell it to you in brief: fish, meat, wine, ritual hand-gestures (mudrā), and sexual union. (63)
The accomplishment of the divine heroes is the accomplishment through the state of being (bhāva).
A brahmin should never drink liquor, nor should he ever consume the mudrā.
Sexual intercourse must not be practiced with those who are forbidden, for it destroys spiritual accomplishment.
The Avadhūta is Śiva himself; the Avadhūta is Sadāśiva.
The goddess Avadhūtī is auspicious, and the stage of life of the Avadhūta is great.
Furthermore, the Avadhūta is of two kinds: the householder and the one who follows what is beneficial. (66)
He is both clothed and naked, dwelling in the source of all ordinances; he is always with his wife yet eternally alone, laughing half a laugh while appearing as one who wears no clothes.
O Goddess of the gods, Sadāśiva is the second [form] who has shaken off the household life;
O lady of excellent complexion, in the Kali age there is no direct practice of wine as a means of realization.
One who has renounced the household life should act everywhere as a naked ascetic;
for this very reason, O lady of excellent hips, one should adopt a mixed mode of conduct.
Whoever worships Kālikā with such a mixture of conduct, she—the sustainer of the world and the bestower of the path to liberation—will be satisfied. (70)
Enjoyment is within one's own hand, and liberation is within one's own hand;
by the grace of the Goddess’s mantra, what on this earth is not accomplished? (71)
O Pārvatī, the lotus feet of Tāriṇī are the refuge for the gods, the asuras, and the kinnaras, and they bestow liberation.
With *japā*, *aparājitā*, *droṇa*, and red oleanders (*karavīra*), with fragrances, *bilva* leaves, and various kinds of food offerings (*naivedya*). (73)
In this manner, the ritual procedure, which consists of bringing about the perfection of action, must be performed;
at that very moment, one becomes perfected, liberated while living, and eternally auspicious (Sadāśiva).
Coconut water and fresh water accomplish all goals;
having placed them in a bronze vessel and molasses in the left hand, one should perform the ritual visualization of the cause.
Then, O daughter of the mountain, worship should be performed with liquor;
[the goddesses] Brāhmaṇī, Kṣatriyā, Vaiśyā, Śūdrāṇī, and Sarvamaṅgalā [are to be worshipped]. (76)
White, red, yellow, and black are declared to be auspicious;
white flowers are for the Brāhmaṇa, while red flowers are for the Kṣatriya.
For a Vaiśya, yellow flowers are prescribed, and for a Śūdra, black; thus it has been declared.
Between the consciousness [of wine] and the liquor of spirits, the consciousness alone is superior. (78)
He should not offer other substitutes, nor should he give mere liquor alone;
by the drinking of *saṃvid* alone, he is a hero and a drinker of wine. (79)
O Daughter of the Mountain, that which is declared in the *Vāgjāla-śāstra* is forbidden; one should not accept its words, but rather accept the speech consisting of the Tantras. (80)
Śivā is the creator, Śivā is the destroyer, and Śivā is the ordainer of auspiciousness;
this goddess is the auspicious Ramanī, I am Śiva, and she is the beloved of Śiva.
She who is meditated upon by Sadāśiva and Śivarāja, and who bestows the bliss of Śiva—
by means of her, the bliss of Vāmā and the bliss of Śiva, a person becomes equal to Bhava himself.
O fair-faced one, knowing the reality of these three states, one should meditate in this way.
[Thus ends the second chapter in the Muṇḍamālā Tantra, in the dialogue between Pārvatī and Īśvara.]
[Now the third chapter:
Seated upon the peak of Kailāsa, adorned with a crescent moon,
Pārvatī addressed the three-eyed God with supreme devotion.
O Lord, I desire to hear the many tantras that have been widely disseminated. || 1 ||
Śrīparvatī said:
O God of gods, Mahādeva, deliverer from the ocean of worldly existence!
Salutations to you, O God, Lord of gods, blue-throated one, three-eyed one! 2.
Salutations to you, O Lord of Pārvatī; salutations to the Master of the ten sciences.
O Bearer of the Gaṅgā, O Sovereign of the World, O Lord Śaṅkara, O Hara! 3.

O Support of the entire world without remainder, O Supportless One, O Effortless One; O Seedless One, O You who are beyond description as possessing qualities, yet the end-maker of those with qualities, O Lord! (4)
Salutations to you, O support of victory, Lord of victory, whose very nature is triumph;
O bliss of victory, O contentment, O beloved of the life-breath of Vijayā!
O Lord of the world, O one worthy of worship by the world, victory to you, O Lord, O Sovereign of the universe!
O Viśvanātha, be gracious; O Śaṅkara, be well-pleased.
Śrī Śiva said: There are seventy million great vidyās and likewise secondary vidyās;
there are ten million mantras of Śrī Viṣṇu and ten million mantras of Śiva.
Śūdras have the right to practice [this path] excluding the word "svāhā" and the syllable "praṇava.
O Maheśvarī, this path is difficult for all to attain; it is a path hard to traverse.
O Dear One, for the devotees of Śakti, He is indeed easier to attain than the easiest;
there is no deity higher than Him, and there is no happiness greater than this.
There is no knowledge higher than this, nor any state higher than this;
listen, O Goddess, O lady of beautiful hips, to that which is dearer than the highest.
If the practitioner, relying solely upon the right and the left [channels], should meditate upon the supreme Vidyā, he becomes the Lord of Umā; of this there is no doubt. (11)
Listen, O Caṇḍī, O lady of excellent limbs, O you with a formidable face, O you who are clad in the directions!
He praises you constantly with devotion; salutations to you, O Mother of the World! (12)
The illustrious Śiva said:
O you with terrible fangs and a formidable face, who are fond of wine, meat, and offerings;
O destroyer of Caṇḍa and Muṇḍa, adorned with a garland of severed heads!
Salutations to you, O Mahāmāyā; salutations to Durgā, the rider of the buffalo!
Salutations to you, the beloved of the Lord of the Universe, the source of all auspiciousness! 14.
I shall indeed declare the supreme reality, the essence of essences, higher than the highest.
Listen, O Goddess, Mother of the World; attend with full attention. (15)
The section on Yonimudrā was previously described by me;
the triangle, endowed with the three qualities, is the womb, the supreme cause.
If one associates with him perceiving him as Śiva, he becomes Śiva himself; of this there is no doubt.
Just as rice remains bound by its husk, yet becomes pure grain when the husk is removed. (17)
Bound by karma the individual soul (jīva) becomes [mortal]; liberated from karma, it is Sadāśiva.
For living beings, the experience of karma is the supreme affliction and is most terrible. (18)
Therefore, one should worship Tārā, the mother of the world, with a spirit of devotion;
she is the supreme purifier, wearing matted hair, ashes, and a tiger skin. (19)
That lord of practitioners who recites [the mantra] continuously upon the surface of the earth is blessed, he is a poet, a hero, divine, and a supreme being. || 20 ||
Purity of being, purity of knowledge, and supreme purity joined together;
purity of consciousness, purity of the seat, and purity of meditation which is truly auspicious. (21)
Having truly realized the supreme reality— knowledge which is the sole means to liberation—
the individual soul, through supreme intellect, shall attain the state of Śiva.
He who brings about the union with Sadāśiva within the beautiful abode of the Mother of the World in the Sahasrāra is a wise man. (23)
And I shall joyfully declare the doctrine of the wise, the doctrine of the wise;
one who is united with both knowledge and ignorance may always wander upon the earth.
The *iḍā* channel is situated on the left, and the moon resides there as well; the *piṅgalā* channel is on the right, and the sun resides there as well. (25)
In the center is the Suṣumnā; within that is the Brahma-nāḍī, which is captivating.
The person who establishes the central void shall become a conqueror of death.

O Goddess of the gods, it is true that when one performs the filling and exhaling of the wind situated in the middle of the *citriṇī* [nāḍī] through the tips of the left nostril, [the result follows].
On the right, however, are Dakṣiṇā, Vāmā, Virāmā, Asitā, and Asitā;
on the left are the channels Kapālā, Vijihvā, and Śūlakāriṇī.
Kaṅkālā and Niṣkalaṅkā, on the left and right respectively,
pierced the wheel in succession— a place unattainable even by the lords of yoga.
In the center of the sky is a delightful wheel of a thousand petals;
there, O beloved, is the charming city of Kālī, which consists of all colors.
Having mentally, intellectually, and physically envisioned her as Caṇḍikā,
he enters into meditation right there and performs the recitation and worship.
O lady of excellent hips, if one practices meditation constantly with joy,
then at that very moment, unfailing perfection and liberation arise.
Neither meditation, nor worship, nor praise is ultimately real;
one should worship that Mother of the World with flowers born of the mind.
Whether in Kāmarūpa, in the house of a brahmin, or even in the home of a dog-cooker (śvapaca),
the purifying liberation that occurs at Gaṅgādvāra and Prayāga comes to one's very mouth.
Wherever a man of knowledge dies, right there he shall attain liberation;
such is the merit born of remembering Durgā, such is the fruit born of remembering Durgā.
O Daughter of the Mountain, what on earth cannot be accomplished simply by the remembrance of Durgā—whether one be a Śaiva, a Vaiṣṇava, or even a Śākta? (37)
One should worship Durgā, remember Durgā, and conquer Durgā, the beloved of Śiva;
at that very moment, O Goddess of the lords of gods, one is liberated from the bondage of worldly existence.
Just as [milk] extracted from milk is not [identical to it] when thrown back into it, nor does it remain as before;
so too, the self (ātman) is said here to be distinct from the qualities (guṇas). (39)
Just as water mixed with milk becomes milk itself, so too there would be no distinction between the individual self (jīvātman) and the supreme self (paramātman). || 40 ||
Just as the disks of the moon and sun appear in jars filled with water,
when the jar is broken, the moon and sun dissolve back into the waters themselves.
The supreme Śiva, the Self, is neither born nor does it die;
having attained the knowledge of the Self, one crosses over the ocean of saṃsāra. (42)
Thus, O fierce goddess, the living soul always crosses over and attains the state of Śiva;
by worshipping the pair of Pārvatī’s feet, one becomes a Kinnara.
Why should heaven, enjoyment, and liberation not belong to the Śāktas?
Indeed, those lowest of men who utter insults against the Śāktas [reap the consequences]. (44)
The terrifying hosts indeed drink their blood;
both the Bhairavas and the Bhairavis always slaughter the base ones.
Those who drink much blood indeed drink their blood; they strike down the devotees of Śakti, roar, revile, and engage in much idle chatter.
O Goddess of the gods, beloved of Śiva, she shatters their heads;
there is no one superior to the Śāktas in heaven, on earth, or in the netherworld. 47.
Śaṅkara, who possesses power (śākta), should be known as the three-eyed one with the moon upon his crest;
having himself become the bearer of the Gaṅgā, he shall sport upon the circle of the earth. 48.
There is no scripture equal to the Tantra; there is no devotee superior to Keśava; there is no yogi like Śaṅkara; and there is no deity higher than Durgā. 49.
If it is diminished in the southern part, one should cast it outward below the chest;
its movement is death, yet when accompanied by the *palāṅka* and half of *kheda*, it bestows liberation.
You have heard the multitude of Durgā’s mantras in various tantras;
however, this particular mantra has not been spoken of anywhere, nor have you ever heard it.
O Caṇḍī, that person who constantly worships the supreme mantra consisting of the name "Durgā, Durgā, Durgā" is liberated while living. (52)
In a great portent, in a most terrible [calamity], in a great misfortune,
in a crisis, in great suffering, in great grief, when great fear has arisen— (53)
O Goddess of the gods, he who constantly remembers Durgā and who recites the supreme mantra shall attain the state of Nīlakaṇṭha in this world of living beings.
The individual soul is Śiva; Śivā is Vāmā, the delightful one, O daughter of Śiva.
Having thus adopted this state of being and being endowed with ritual action and devotion, [one should worship]. || 55 ||
It is thus: where is there suffering, or where is fear, or where is hell?
Where is the Kali age and where is Time? His entire body consists of nothing but truth. (56)
O beautiful one, the life-story of Kālī, Tārā, Tripurā, Bhairavī, and Bhuvanā bestows liberation. || 57 ||
Having attained that very state of being, by which one may go to the bed of liberation—which consists of knowledge, is ever-gratifying, and destroys all suffering—[one should remain there]. || 58 ||
The recitation of the Goddess Pārvatī, the worship of the station of Pārvatī, and taking refuge in the feet of the Goddess Pārvatī—which destroy worldly existence—[are the means]. (59)
She is Kālī because she restrains Time (Kāla), and Karālā because she crushes her enemies;
therefore, by worshipping her feet, one will certainly become the son of the Goddess. 60.
O Caṇḍī, various and diverse modes of conduct have been previously described;
now, O Śaṅkarī, listen with your mind to the account of the sacrifice.
One should meditate upon the goddess Durgā, the destroyer of misfortune, within the heart-lotus—
fierce, with terrible fangs, and adorned with a garland of severed heads.
One should meditate upon Tāriṇī, mounted upon a corpse, situated in a cremation ground, naked,
with a half-smile and a protruding tongue, dark as a rain cloud, and bestowing boons.
He who constantly remembers Bhavānī at the end [of his life] becomes the Lord of Pārvatī;
he beholds the Liṅga situated in the thousand-spoked [lotus], possessing the luster of molten gold.
When is it white, when black, yellow, or blue, and when is it?
When is the Liṅga composed of colors and adorned with vowels and other [phonemes]? (65)
The Liṅga situated in the center of the lotus consists of light and is beyond thought;
the Liṅga, adorned by the individual soul (jīva) and other principles, is established upon the pericarp.
Then, endowed with devotion, one should prostrate to Sadāśiva with devotion;
at that time, one attains perfection, and not otherwise even in ten million kalpas.
O Great Goddess, what is the use of much speaking? Success is achieved through devotion to the Guru. || 67 ||
[Thus ends the third chapter in the Muṇḍamālā Tantra, in the dialogue between Pārvatī and Īśvara. || 3 ||
[Then the Fourth Chapter] The Goddess said:
O illustrious one, lord of yoga, compassionate toward devotees, I ask you one thing.
I ask about the supreme reality, O God of gods, Sadāśiva.
Śrī Śiva said:
O Mother of the World, I shall narrate the life-story of Durgā; listen.
Durgā, the sustainer of the world, is one, and indeed the Supreme Śiva is one.
And those beings who are portions of me are Śaivas; there is no doubt in this.
And those who are portions of you are Śāktas; this is indeed the truth, O daughter of the mountain.
At the end of many thousands of years, O Goddess, there will be Śaivas devoted to Śakti,
and Śāktas who follow Śaṅkara, regardless of whose lineage they may have originated from.
Cāṇḍālas, Brāhmaṇas, Śūdras, Kṣatriyas, and those born as Vaiśyas—these, O Mother of the World, are devotees of Śakti; they are never merely human beings.
People in this world perceive [him] merely with the physical eye;
yet any human being whatsoever may remember him, whether with faith or even without faith.
Having crossed over hundreds of difficulties, he attains the supreme goal,
just as Indra, Kubera, Varuṇa, and the practitioner [attain theirs].
And likewise, in this world, a practitioner devoted to the worship of Durgā—
whoever remembers the consort of Rudra, whether with devotion or even without devotion— [attains success].
Having enjoyed happiness in this world, O Daughter of the Mountain, he shall go to the abode of Śiva; indeed, in this very life, he may attain heaven, hell, or liberation.
In this world, however, one's dwelling shall be within the universe consisting of all powers;
O wife of Bhava, listen now to the hundred names of Durgā.
Durgā, Bhavānī, Queen of the Gods, Śivā, beloved of Viśvanātha;
she who has terrible fangs, a formidable mouth, and is adorned with a garland of skulls.
Rudrāṇī, Tāriṇī, Tārā, Māheśī, Bhavavallabhā, Nārāyaṇī, Jagaddhātrī, Mahādevapriyā, and Jayā. (12)
Vijayā, Jayārādhyā, Śarvāṇī, Haravallabhā, Asitā, the goddess Aṇimā, Laghimā, and likewise Garimā. (13)
She is the power of Maheśa, the sovereign of the universe, Gaurī, the daughter of the mountain;
she is eternal, stainless, desireless, and perpetually fresh.
Red in color, with a red face, Vāṇī is endowed with the eight treasures (vasu) and bestows the treasures;
she is dear to Rāma, devoted to Rāma, and the granter of boons from the Lord of the Raghus. || 15 ||
She is the external sovereign, devoted to the external, dark-complexioned, and the bestower of boons;
she is Yaśodā, Rādhikā, Caṇḍī, Draupadī, and likewise Rukmiṇī.
She who is dear to Guha, who delights in Guha, who sports in the lineage of Guha;
she who is the mother of Gaṇeśa, the Mother, the one whose form is the universe, and Jāhnavī. 17.
Gaṅgā, Kālī, Kāśī, Bhairavī, Bhuvaneśvarī, Nirmalā, Sugandhā, Devakī, and Devapūjitā. (18)
Born of Dakṣa, she is the sacrificial fee (dakṣiṇā), skillful (dakṣā), and the destroyer of Dakṣa’s sacrifice;
she is of excellent character, beautiful, gentle, Mātaṅgī, and whose essence is the lotus (kamalā). || 19 ||
She who destroys Niśumbha, she who destroys Śumbha, she who destroys Caṇḍa;
she who is the destroyer of Dhūmralocana and the crusher of the demon Mahiṣāsura.
Umā, Gaurī, Karālā, Kāminī, Viśvamohanī, Jagadīśapriyā, Janmanāśinī, and Bhavanāśinī. || 21 ||
With a terrible mouth and a lolling tongue, laughing with a loud laugh and naked, the goddess Bhāratī has gone to heaven—she who bestows enjoyment and grants liberation. 22.
Thus, O fair-faced one, these hundred names have been told;
by the mere remembrance of these names, one is liberated while living—of this there is no doubt. (23)
Whoever, having risen at dawn, recites this while remembering the two feet of Durgā, is liberated from the bonds of birth; no doubt should be entertained in this matter. (24)
At the time of attaining success, whether during the day, at night, or at the onset of night,
by reciting these hundred names, one will certainly obtain the perfection of mantra.
If one should obtain the tenfold knowledge without knowing this King of Hymns, there will be no accomplishment whatsoever; this is the truth, the absolute truth, O Maheśvarī. (26)
Having become the beloved of beautiful women in Kāmarūpa, the region of desire, that temple of longing for lovely women, he shall sport upon the circle of the earth. (27)
O lady of excellent complexion, having seated the beautiful woman on his left side,
he should always worship Tāriṇī with his mouth filled with betel.
In the middle of the great night, having placed Vāmalocanā on his left, he recites that mantra, which bestows accomplishment upon all embodied beings. (29)
Beholding the lotus-face of Vāmā, the lover of beautiful countenance lets out a loud laugh, and thereby Durgā becomes pleased.
The supreme Brahman, the supreme abode, the cause of supreme bliss,
eternal bliss, changeless, desireless— the state that is Tāriṇī.
Having meditated [upon her], one attains liberation; this is the truth, O most beautiful one!
As is Durgā, so is Vāmā; as is Vāmā, so is Śivā. (32)
Becoming filled with devotion to Śiva, one should always wander pure;
for who on the surface of the earth is a true Śākta without the pair of Kālī’s feet? (33)
Devoid of power he is manifestly a corpse; endowed with power he is Sadāśiva.
Endowed with power he becomes Viṣṇu, or indeed he is Viṣṇu himself.
O Mother of the Universe, know the royal road to be the path of power (śaktimārga);
no other worship should be performed, nor any praise, nor any meditative visualization.
Neither meditation, nor the perfection of yoga, nor any other mantra is [the goal] for the wise;
rather, it is solely the lotus feet of Kālikā that shatter the bonds of worldly existence.
O Caṇḍī, there is no other god, nor any sacred ford, nor meditation, nor even discourse; there is no wandering to holy sites, nor is there the practice of yoga here.
Praise is Durgā, the intellect is Durgā, and Sadaśiva is the stability that is Durgā;
hunger, sleep, compassion, delusion, and forbearance are Durgā, for she is the ultimate refuge. (38)
Śakti is Śiva, and Śiva is Śakti; Śakti is Brahmā and Janārdana; Śakti is Sūrya and Candra, as well as Kubera and Varuṇa. || 39 ||
He who does not know that the entire universe is of the nature of Śakti is a sinner;
he who knows the world on this earth to be thus composed of Śakti [is virtuous]. 40.
He knows Kālikā, the Mother of the Universe, within the heart of the earth;
he alone is an expert in all scriptures and beloved by all.
One attains accomplishment in the cremation ground; there is no need for deliberation on this point.
An empty house or a cremation ground are equal in the eyes of those most skilled in the supreme [knowledge]. (42)
Or whoever goes there on the fourteenth day or the new moon night, which is dear to Hara, will certainly become Viśveśa himself. (43)
Having recited it ten thousand times, he becomes accomplished in all rites;
he is a lord of yogis, a knower of the true nature of things, and steadfast in all undertakings.
He should be known as eternally blissful and proficient in all duties;
having gone to the root of an Aśvattha tree at dawn, he becomes supremely wise.
One should worship with supreme devotion, even with meat and blood, or with *bola* fruits, *bilva* leaves, or *bilva* flowers, O fair-faced one. (46)
O Daughter of the Mountain, beginning on the fourteenth day, one should recite the mantra a hundred thousand times;
on the fifth day, one should worship the Goddess at the root of a bilva tree day and night.
Then one attains perfection of speech and becomes a Vācaspati, though previously insignificant.
The twelvefold posture is the supreme Saṅketāsana. (48)
The Bhadrapīṭha posture, the Padmāsana, the Siddhāsana, as well as the Siddhasiddhāsana, the Devyāsana, and the Kukkuṭāsana. || 49 ||
The heroic posture (vīrāsana) is supreme, O blessed lady, as is the posture of the bestower of boons;
the lion posture (siṃhāsana) is supreme, O Goddess, and the cemetery posture (śmaśānāsana) is the most excellent.
O lady of excellent limbs, the corpse posture (śavāsana) is difficult even for the gods to attain;
therein one should take refuge in the supreme Brahman, the most excellently adorned posture.
Having placed his wife on his left side, he should worship the consort of Bhava with incense, fragrant perfumes, the chewing of betel, and other such offerings.
O Daughter of Śaṅkara, by praising Bhavānī, the liberating Vidyā, the enchanting Brahmavidyā, one attains liberation at that very moment.
O Mother of the Universe, O Support of Victory, O Sovereign of the Universe, salutations be unto you!
O you of the formidable face, O terrible one, O beloved of the Moon-crested Lord! 54.
Save me, O highly fortunate one; grant me the unsurpassed perfection!
O Kāmeśvarī, you who are the embodiment of the wish-fulfilling vine of desire, whose intellect is the supreme art! 55.
In Kāmarūpa, Vijaya, and Nistāra,
Yaśovāhinī took hold of a corpse-cāṇḍāla, seizing his forehead, face, and head.
Repeatedly grasping and releasing the nose, the two ears, the heart-lotus, the navel, the genitals, the anus, as well as the arms, the back, and the belly; || 57 ||
At the beginning, one should apply the *māyā* syllable, then again *māyā*, and again *māyā*;
likewise, one should place the seed-syllable of the bride (*vadhū*) and the *lajjā* syllable upon every limb of the mantra. (58)
Having recited the mantra one hundred and eight times and performed obeisance to Śiva,
he [should again] with the seed-syllable of movement (vihāra), using the blue substance and his eye.
At that very moment, O Goddess of the gods, it comes to pass; of this there is no doubt.
O Maheśānī, in an empty house, one should face the direction of the Giver of Wealth (the North).
A rosary of conch shells should be taken, or one made of crystal or silver;
or a rosary made of gold, or one fashioned from coral.

Having recited the Kullukā mantra one hundred times at the location of the crown of the head—the unsurpassed [number]—the practitioner of mantra should then recite the mantra; he becomes Maheśa, of this there is no doubt. (62)
He who recites the mantra of Tāriṇī is capable, a devotee of Śiva, Bhairava, and Sadāśiva; he is of noble birth and a knower of the Kula. (63)
She who dwells in the heart-lotus, the sustainer of the world, the sovereign goddess stationed upon the crown of the head;
she who is the serpent-maiden, ever-awake, and adorned with serpents and other ornaments. (64)
Served by Nārada and other foremost practitioners, and frequented by the Siddhas,
[one should worship] at the foot of an Aśvattha tree, at the root of a Bilva tree, or in the house of one's own wife.
One should meditate upon the Goddess, the supreme deity—whether as a passionate woman or otherwise—as the primordial, luminous Vidyā, who is auspicious, bestows boons, and grants fearlessness. (66)
One should bow down with hymns of praise to Caṇḍī, the destroyer of all defects;
whether staying in a cremation ground or established in Śiva, one should recite this supreme armor (kavaca).
Then, O Goddess of gods, O lady of excellent complexion, success will be attained in a cremation ground or upon a corpse; at that time, the Bhairavas of the opposing faction shall not prevail.
The Unmatta, the Krodhana, the Bhairava who is the essence of the Baṭuka, the Saṃhāra, the Bhīṣaṇa, and likewise the Kālabhairava. (69)
And Mahākālabhairava— these indeed are the eight in number (the Vasus)—
having seen the cremation ground, O Goddess of Gods, as well as the practice of the corpse-sādhana.
All the Bhairavas dance and roar with blood-red eyes;
today there shall be one like me, or perhaps even one as mad as the wind.
"Between the corpse and the cremation ground, I do not know how [to proceed]. Do not fear; all the Bhairavas will speak from their bonds. (72)
"Who are these lions, tigers, boars, and others roaring everywhere? Do not fear, do not fear, do not fear, O practitioner! (73)
Or whoever shall speak before [the assembly], he is the Guru, an expert in reality, even without complete knowledge of the Tantra and without having served a Guru. (74)
Without breath control, without meditation, without the recitation of mantras, without knowledge, without ritual placement (nyāsa), and without binding the corpse; || 75 ||
Without existence, without gain, without the service of the company of the virtuous;
without recitation, without austerity, and even without the temple of desire. (76)
O Goddess of the gods, the beloved of Hara is not accomplished through direct perception;
O Goddess, it is only by the power of fortune that the beloved of Hara becomes manifest to direct perception.
At that very moment, success arises and the Mahāvidyā becomes propitious. || 77 ||
[Thus ends the fourth chapter in the Muṇḍamālā Tantra, in the dialogue between Pārvatī and Īśvara. || 4 ||
[Now begins the fifth chapter:
Once, the goddess Pārvatī, residing in her abode on Kailāsa,
laughing aloud, spoke with a faltering voice.
Śrī Pārvatī said:
O God of gods, Mahādeva, Lord of the universe, Sadāśiva!
O Sovereign of the world, I ask you about the grinding of my temple.
O Lord, O Maheśvara, of what nature is that Brahman consisting of Śiva and Śakti, whose body is composed of eternal bliss, and at what time does it appear? || 3 ||
O Lord Viśveśvara, I have heard about the worship of the nine maidens;
O God, by your grace, I have also heard about the worship of the Kumārīs.
Śrī Śiva said:
There are twelve kinds of erotic sentiment (śṛṅgāra), four kinds of the reverse (viparīta),
and four kinds pertaining to the devotees of Śiva, as well as those found in new hands.
O Sovereign of All, he who does not know this is a beast; of this there is no doubt.
This must not be revealed before a beast; it must not be revealed under any circumstances.
But a beast is a cruel enemy that destroys all states of being,
O Consort of Śaṅkara, even in a hundred million aeons or even in a single year.
O Sovereign of the Universe, it is not accomplished; I tell you the truth, the absolute truth:
he who does not know the beauty of the erotic sentiment is no scholar.
He is a fool, fallen from power in all the scriptures; of this there is no doubt—just as the bliss of Śakti arises in the beauty of the erotic sentiment (śṛṅgāra-rasa).
O Maheśānī, such bliss is not produced in any way whatsoever within the Śaiva, Vaiṣṇava, Saura, or Gāṇapatya [traditions].
Śiva is birth, Śiva is the body, Śiva is dharma, Śiva is pleasure;
Śiva is the creator, Śiva is the protector, Śiva is the destroyer—he whose very nature is Śiva. || 11 ||
Śiva is intellect, Śiva is peace, Śiva is the goal, Śiva is thought;
Śiva is action, Śiva is power, Śiva is liberation, whose very nature is Śiva.
"I am Śiva, there is no doubt in this; I am indeed the living soul that is Śiva himself"—O Daughter of the Mountain, he in whose mind such a thought dwells [is liberated]. (13)
At that very moment, accomplishment and infallible liberation arise;
O Vārārohā, on the path of Śakti, the Avadhūta is Śaṅkara himself.
He for whom the *avadhūtī* is on the left becomes himself an *avadhūta*;
wherever his dwelling may be, that is Kailāsa—of this there is no doubt. (15)
His temple is Kailāsa, and its pillar is known to be made of jewels;
O Śivā, beloved of all, even the trees and the mountains are considered small [in comparison]. 16.
The Kṣudras, Bāndhavas, Rudras, Supradhānas, Sadāśivas, Bhairavas, Kiṅkaras—all of them—and the Bhairavīs, Ceṭikās, and so forth. (17)
Thus is the supreme abode of Kailāsa, which brings joy to all,
captivating to the mind, consisting of bliss, and likewise filled with universal peace.

O beloved, he who shall indeed behold this bliss—which is dear to all, composed of all virtues, the source of all happiness and the like, and thus consisting of everything—[shall attain liberation]. 19.
Having become endowed with all powers, one should wander upon the circle of the earth;
on the eighth or ninth day of the dark fortnight, one should mutter [the mantra] ten thousand times at night.
Then, preceded by the proper time for mantra practice, one attains success;
thus the ritual should be performed, for it is remembered as being most secret when kept hidden.
Secret worship is more secret than the [public] rite; it destroys success.
They are considered Śākta within, Śaiva without, and Vaiṣṇava in the assembly. (22)
Kaulas, assuming various forms, wander upon the surface of the earth;
such is the Tantra heard to have arisen from this ritual procedure, which is delusive.
The knowledge of the family has been heard by the noble one; the Heart of the Yoginīs has been heard;
the Sammohana-vīratantra has been heard, as well as the supreme Śrītantra. (24)
Likewise, the Kulārṇava, the Kālītantra, the Kālīvilāsaka, and the Śrīkālīkalpalatikā were heard with the highest reverence. (25)
And when there is a difference of opinion, that worship remains hidden, destroying its manifestation.
O fair-faced one, they are Śākta within, Śākta without, and Śākta in their ritual action.
O Maheśvarī, those empowered by devotion, those empowered by desire, those empowered by meditation,
those empowered by passion, and those empowered by the Śakti— there is no other way in any ritual actions.
O Śaṅkarī, those who are Śaivas within and Śivas without, whether in an assembly or at home,
are likewise Vaiṣṇavas at all times.
Thus has the supreme state been declared among all wombs;
having taken recourse to this state, the Śāktas are the supreme worshippers. (29)
All are composed of eternal bliss, three-eyed, and have the moon as their crest-jewel;
they always sport with Śakti and are perpetually immersed in supreme joy.
He should be known as ever-joyful and skilled in all actions—those who dwell upon the earth by taking refuge in the dharma of their own lineage. 31.
By virtue of the family dharma, they become auspicious and their lives become auspicious;
Śaṅkara is himself noble by birth, and Hari is likewise noble by birth.
The god Vāsava is of noble birth, and the Grandfather (Brahmā) is likewise of noble birth;
all the sages are of noble birth, and the ancestors are traditionally held to be of noble birth.
Kinnaras and those of noble lineage, men who live by tending cattle, asuras and those of noble lineage—these are born of noble families, yet they are not truly "of noble character. (34)
Therefore, there is never devotion nor liberation for the Asuras;
nor for the Rākṣasas, the noble-born, nor those born of Gandharvas, Apsarases, and Yakṣas. (35)
Having established devotion to the Goddess, one attains fulfillment upon the earth;
yet without the full realization of Durgā, worship and recitation are fruitless. (36)
If purity were to come from the practice of austerity, then all this would be useless;
for whether one is a fool or a scholar, O lady of beautiful countenance, [it would matter only if one were a Brahmin]. (37)
O lady of excellent complexion, whether one is a Kṣatriya, born of a Vaiśya, a Śūdra, or even a Caṇḍāla, all are equal and empowered by Śakti; for this is the means of accomplishing all goals. (38)
Listen, O Goddess, O lady of excellent hips, to my most certain words;
he is an expert in all rites, possessing the beauty of the erotic sentiment. (39)
From the erotic sentiment (śṛṅgāra) creation is born; from the erotic sentiment delight is born;
Śaṅkara is pleased by the erotic sentiment, O Pārvatī, and even from the erotic sentiment [all things arise]. 40.
O fair-faced one, you are contented and I too am indeed contented;
O Goddess of the Suras, whether it be the word of love (śṛṅgāra) that is graceful or harsh, [it is pleasing]. 41.
By the mere word "erotic" (śṛṅgāra), people shall attain the supreme goal;
for women are goddesses, women are life itself, and women alone are indeed the ornament. 42.
One should never harbor hatred toward women; O Goddess of the gods, one should avoid censuring them or striking them, even if one is devoid of compassion and shame. (43)
He who on the surface of the earth knows the female form to be the form of Tāriṇī,
he should be known as the husband of women, and he alone is the husband of Pārvatī.
On a Tuesday, a Saturday, a Thursday, or likewise on a Friday, one should worship with a spirit of devotion on either the third or the second lunar day. (45)
O Śāṅkarī, either a person endowed with devotion, or even Janārdana himself, [worships] the primordial Goddess composed of light, or the fourth [form]. || 46 ||
One should worship the fifth Vidyā, adorned with the fifth [syllable];
one should worship Durgā, the beloved of the five-faced one, with a spirit of devotion. || 47 ||
O Varārohā, this ritual practice is of the nature of sattva, as well as rajas;
and it is also of the nature of tamas, O Goddess of gods—thus has the worship been heard, O Maheśvarī. (48)
Whatever worship has been described, all that worship has been heard by you;
now [learn] the worship of Śaṅkara with the kuṇḍa-flower and the gola-flower.
O Pārvatī, O Goddess of the gods, one should worship the beloved of Hara with Cakrapuṣpa, Śūla, Vajrapuṣpa, and Kālapuṣpa flowers. (50)
Then one attains perfection; this is the truth, the truth, there is no doubt.
A living being devoted to the path of the Kula is Śiva himself, there is no doubt. (51)
A living being intent on the purpose of the family dharma should wander upon the path of the family;
relying upon the flower of the family, he should take recourse in the stage of life of the noble-born. || 52 ||
In the Kali age, fish, meat, liquor, ritual gestures, and sexual union—just as the divine is so is the hero; there is no difference between them, O lady of pure smiles. (53)
Even from consuming the fifth [type of food], no fault arises for men;
however, that which is impossible for the weak to perform increases all [types of] rebirth.
Drinking liquor is not to be done, it is not to be done in the Kali age;
yet for the Śāktas, indeed for the Śāktas, it is to be performed as that which bestows all accomplishments.
Or else, taking refuge in a great seat (mahāpīṭha) or beholding a great seat,
one should worship the Goddess in that great seat, endowed with supreme devotion.
One should worship with red flowers, red perfumes and ointments,
as well as with bilva leaves, maṇi flowers, and campaka flowers.
One should worship the Goddess with red lotuses, red garlands, and ornaments of red hue, as well as with buffaloes, medicinal herbs, and even blood.
O beautiful one, your worship is performed according to this prescribed ritual with the blood from the limbs of goats, as well as that of Brahmins. 59.
O Maheśvarī, the domestic rites (gṛhya) must be performed by you among the worlds of the twice-born;
thus, O Sovereign of the Three Worlds, your worship is to be ordained.
Then, having become a Lord of Siddhas (Siddhīśvara), he shall attain the status of a leader of the Gaṇas (Gāṇapatya).
O Goddess of the Gods, this divine [teaching] of mine must not be revealed before one who is a mere bound soul (paśu).
By the mere sight of the sacrificial animal, the purities of the heroes are destroyed;
mental worship, however, bestows great siddhi and grants liberation. 62.
The external worship, which consists of the inner sacrifice, destroys the state of being a mere living soul; it is rajasic and bestows all prosperity.
It bestows both worldly enjoyment and liberation, destroys all calamities, causes the exhaustion of all defects, and annihilates all enemies. || 64 ||
It causes the destruction of all diseases and brings liberation from all bonds;
for heroes and sacrificial animals alike, external worship is the lowest of the low.
"O Goddess, in the Toḍala-yāmala, it has been heard in detail that among all divine [forms of worship], external worship is the lowest. (66)
Nevertheless, O daughter of the mountain, I have described this worship in brief;
through the recitation of praise, through firm knowledge, and through worship, O beautiful lady of Śiva, [the goal is attained]. 67.
The Great Vidyā is perfectly propitious; through recitation, success will arise.
From recitation comes devotion, from recitation comes enjoyment, from recitation comes liberation, and from recitation comes spiritual action.
O Goddess of the Gods, through recitation one gains the Tantra; through recitation, the Mantra; through recitation, the Yantra.
Through recitation comes splendor; through recitation, peace; through recitation, faith; and through recitation, compassion. (69)

From recitation comes contentment; from recitation, nourishment; from recitation, the goal; from recitation, intelligence; from recitation, wisdom; from recitation, prosperity; from recitation, birth; and from recitation, stability.
Peace comes from recitation, peace comes from recitation, peace comes from recitation; of this there is no doubt. || 70 ||
[Thus ends the fifth chapter in the Muṇḍamālā Tantra, in the dialogue between Pārvatī and Īśvara. || 5 ||
[Now begins the sixth chapter.
The Goddess said:
"O Mahādeva, I have previously heard about the means of accomplishing the corpse (śavasādhana)."
O Lord, I have heard the sādhana of the cremation ground with the utmost reverence.
O Lord, neither the hymn nor the armor has been heard by me for the purpose of achieving power;
yet, O Mahādeva, O Śaṅkara, [it is achieved] through the armor and indeed through the hymn alone.
O Lord, how may success be attained? Tell me now the armor-mantra (kavaca).
The illustrious Śiva said: Listen, O Goddess, O lady of excellent hips, O Durgā, O most beautiful one;
for the sake of attaining perfection, there is the application of this armor through its binding power.
May Siddheśvarī protect the attainment of success; may Kālikā protect the head;
may Kāminī protect the skull; and may Nageśvarī protect the forehead and the eyes.
May Viśveśvarī protect my ears; may Jagadambikā protect my heart;
may Kālī always protect my face; and may Nīlasarasvatī protect my tongue.
May the goddess Sureśvarī, with her formidable face, protect my hands;
may Himātmajā always protect my teeth, private parts, nails, and navel.
May Nārāyaṇī protect my cheek, and Gaṇḍā always protect my temple; may Bhadrakālī protect my hair, and Durgā, the sovereign of the gods, protect [my head].
May Caṇḍī protect my manhood; may Dhaneśvarī protect my wealth;
may Viśveśvarī protect my breasts; and may Jagadīśvarī protect my entire body. (8)
May Ugratārā always protect [me]; may Mahānīla Sarasvatī protect [me];
may Mahāmāyā protect my tongue; and may Jagadambikā protect my back. (9)
May the Mistress of the Universe protect [me] eternally in the cremation ground;
may Śarvāṇī protect me on the corpse, and may Caṇḍikā always grant protection.
May Kātyāyanī, who carries the corpse, protect the family always;
and may Pārvatī, with her terrible fangs and formidable mouth, protect [us] forever.
"May Kamalā protect my kingdom, and likewise may Mantreśvarī protect my counsel.
Thus, O Goddess, is this armor (kavaca), which is difficult even for the gods to obtain. 12.
O Goddess, whoever recites this constantly shall certainly attain perfection;
if one should recite this armor-mantra when the time for perfection has arrived.
O Goddess, he who undertakes the pursuit of perfection without knowing the armor-mantra (kavaca),
may indeed attain perfection, yet he shall have neither liberation nor the state of the righteous.
Therefore, O Mahāmāyā, this armor-granting [mantra] is difficult to obtain for gods, humans, and kinnaras alike. 15.
Having recited the armor-mantra (kavaca), O Caṇḍī, one shall swiftly attain success;
[especially] in the case of great portents, great suffering, great calamity, or distress.
O Goddess, one should recite this armor-mantra; having recited it, one shall attain liberation, whether in an empty house, a cremation ground, or at Kāmarūpa or Mahāghaṭa.
Whether in his own left chamber or in the temple of Kāma, the practitioner of mantra, endowed with supreme devotion and intelligence, should recite the mantra. (18)

The best of practitioners should recite [the mantra] with the conviction that it is his very life-breath, using his mind, at the root, on a leaf, or on a fruit; likewise at the stalk, at the time, in the wind, in impurity, in water, or on a cloth. (19)
Then, O Maheśvarī, having purified the channels (nāḍī) and purified one's state of being (bhāva),
one who is skilled in the meaning of all scriptures should sport within the center of Hari.
Having ascended the funeral pyre, the Lord of Siddhas attains the state of Nīlakaṇṭha;
the Kānāḍī flows in the left, while indeed the Jāhnavī flows in the right.
In the center is the *kulācala* channel, rare upon the surface of the earth;
likewise, there are the *citriṇī*, *padminī*, *śaṅkhā*, *vijṛmbhā*, and *śoṇadā*.
Kaṅkāla, Kūṭajā, Nāḍī, Kapola, Golajā, and Khalā—
these reside within one's own body, taking their support from the Brahma-nāḍī.
Among all those within the earth, Gaurī, Sūkṣmā, Tāriṇī, Ghaṇṭākarṇā, Lolajihvā, Vikaṭā, and Candravallabhā [are foremost]. || 24 ||
Mahānīlā, Vīrabhadrā, Sulajjā, Nakhadā, Śubhā, Balākā, Kākinī, Rākā, Kālaghaṇṭā, Śivā, and Sitā. || 25 ||
Dardurā, Durārādhyā, Viśokavadanā, Anaghā, Jambhinī, Pukkasā, Śoṇā, Yaśodā, Makhadā, and Khadā. (26)
Khagā, Kharavatī, Nāḍī, Kolā, Helā, Halāhalā, as well as Iḍā, Piṅgalā, and Suṣumnā, who is primordial and formless. (27)
Gāndhārī and Koṭarākṣī are of noble birth and wise in their lineage;
Kanakhalā is the channel (nāḍī) on the left, and Kāmapālikā is on the right.
The abode of Nīlakaṇṭha, which is difficult even for the gods to attain;
Viśvaṃbharā, Kāmā, Karālā, and Meghavāhinī are in his lap. (29)
Ghanabhā, Ghanadā, Caṇḍī, Suśīlā, Varapaṇḍitā, Viśvāraṇyā, Viśvavasanī, Bahupādā, and Kaṭākṣajā. (30)
Nandinī, Śoṇadā, Gaṅgā, Kāśī, and Kamalavāsinī—if one thus meditates upon Mahāmāyā, who is worshipped by the gods, [one attains success]. (31)
At that very moment, accomplishment arises; this is the truth, the truth, there is no doubt.
The terrible, many-legged Katā, which pierces through the clouds, has been conquered.
Through contact with the movement within the channels (nāḍī), one is undoubtedly liberated while living;
listen, O Goddess, who are of terrible luster, fearsome appearance, and clad in the directions as your garment! (33)
By the grace of the wish-fulfilling gem, what on earth cannot be accomplished?
[This occurs] at the root in the four-petalled lotus and at the Svādhiṣṭhāna in the six-petalled [lotus]. (34)
O Maheśvarī, in the Maṇipūra, the Anāhata, and the Ājñā-cakra— thus,
by means of the [mantras] assigned to these wheels numbering ten, twelve, and sixteen [syllables respectively].
O Goddess, where the syllable *maṅku-ra* is placed with its petals, it is considered equal to a hundred cows;
there is Kālīpura, which is served even by Brahmā and the other gods. (36)
To the blue-throated Lord of the three worlds, who dwells within the thousand-petaled lotus,
the master of ten million and the master of millions of lineages, who is beautifully adorned by the foremost of practitioners.
One who is deeply disenchanted with the world should meditate upon the supreme purifier, the Divine;
for the individual soul (jīva) is to be known as Śiva, the Lord of the Universe, who is ever-delighting. (38)
O lady of excellent hips, the reality of Brahman is difficult to attain even for the gods;
it is the Linga established in the vowels and adorned with vowels and consonants. (39)
The Linga, adorned with garlands of letters, beautifying the world, is the Great Seed, resounded by great energies, and is the Supreme Self.
One should meditate upon and worship with mind and speech the god Mahādeva, the blue-throated one, who is always accompanied by Śakti. || 41 ||
At that very moment, the practitioner in this world becomes devoted to the internal sacrifice;
O Mahāmāyā, the internal sacrifice is inaccessible even to other practitioners.
The universe is indeed the body of all living beings;
whatever qualities exist in the universe, those reside within the physical frame. (43)
The body is composed of the *tattvas*, overflowing with various aesthetic flavors (*rasas*);
it is joined with the lunar drop (*candrabindu*) and adorned by the sound-drop (*nādabindu*). || 44 ||
Even the body of Śaṅkara, which bestows liberation, is difficult to attain;
O Mahāmāyā, as long as liberation has not been reached, so long indeed must the practitioner persevere.
For that long, ritual action, enjoyment, and liberation remain unfailing;
yet in this most terrible state of universal affliction, the body is the very station of Brahman.
Having taken the purified flower and all that is born of the body arising from the limbs,
[he should worship] the goddess Kālikā, who is adorned with a garland of severed heads.
One should worship with supreme devotion; he is indeed Śiva himself, there is no doubt.
[He is] the form fashioned from the cosmic egg (brahmāṇḍa), adorned with armlets and other ornaments. 48.
One who is filled with supreme bliss, accompanied by his own Śakti, should worship her who has four arms, a flickering tongue, and is endowed with various powers. 49.
O Goddess of the Gods, on the left [should be placed] one's own left [consort], adorned with various ornaments;
O Goddess of the Gods, for the Kula-cakra, one should recite [the mantra], being equal to Śiva.
At night, with disheveled hair and naked, he should assume the Karālāsya form and recite [the mantra] a thousand or even ten thousand times in the temple of Madana.
Whether it be white or even red, one should offer a flower accompanied by the fifth [note] to Mahākālī according to this prescribed ritual procedure.
O Maheśvarī, worship should be performed during the day, worship at night, and worship at the twilights; by doing so, one shall attain success.
One should never worship the Mother of the World during the day, nor during the night, nor at the junction of day and night; rather, one should worship her with total devotion.
One should not worship the Goddess by day, nor indeed by night;
one should always worship the Goddess, avoiding both day and night.
Just as through the contact of the movement within the channels—namely the iḍā, the piṅgalā, and the suṣumnā which pierces through to Brahman—the practitioner attains liberation. (56)
Without knowledge of the channels, without the cultivation of the channels, and without the All-Creator, O Goddess, there is no success on this earth. (57)
Holding a bilva fruit in his left hand and a rosary in his right hand, the practitioner should recite the mantra of Pārvatī on this earth for the accomplishment of all undertakings. 58.
Having bowed with devotion to the Goddess of gods, who has terrible fangs, a formidable mouth, a loud laugh, and is naked, one should mutter the Cintāmaṇi mantra.
By the grace of the wish-fulfilling gem, what on earth cannot be accomplished?
Having grasped the supreme and auspicious wish-fulfilling gem and the wish-granting creeper (kalpalatā), [what remains unattained]? (60)
O Caṇḍī, by reciting the Great Mantra, one becomes the Lord of the Gods;
O lady of excellent complexion, the individual soul attains the state of Śiva through knowledge.
O Goddess, the lotus feet of the Guru are a most wonderful secret; so too are the beautiful lotus feet of Pārvatī and Śaṅkara, which are truly marvelous.
One should cultivate unity according to the prescribed method; for he alone is truly liberated while living.
O fair-faced one, those who are united with the body, united with the state, and united with the form [attain this].
And those devotees who have transcended the qualities (guṇas) are liberated; of this there is no doubt. || 63 ||
Śrī Pārvatī said:
"O best of gods, I do not know the piṇḍa, the pada, nor the form.
O ocean of mercy, let the certain and supreme doctrine be told to me. (64)
Śrī Śiva said:
O Goddess, I shall speak to you one essential truth, more secret than the most secret:
the *piṇḍa* is proclaimed to be the power Kuṇḍalinī, and the *pada* is the Haṃsa.
O lady of excellent hips, even form is indeed meditation, there is no doubt;
for he who worships the goddess Mahākuṇḍalinī, the serpent-like one.
He has accomplished his purpose; he is blessed; he is a god and the best of heroes;
he is virtuous, a practitioner, and wise; he is honorable and a scholar.
He who performs this will certainly attain the status of a deity throughout the entire universe;
so too shall those divine lords of practitioners, those heroes, and the most excellent of adepts. (68)

The sacrificial animals should be known as animals [only in name], being experts in the meaning of all scriptures; having established themselves in purity of intention, they are skilled in accomplishing every purpose. (69)
The practitioner attains liberation; this is the truth, the absolute truth, O fair-faced one!
Listen, O Goddess, Mother of the World, to that which is the most auspicious of all auspicious things. (70)
O Goddess of gods, one who listens to the Tantra shall attain the nirvāṇa of Brahman;
O Maheśvarī, joined with a woman (vāmā), one should recite the mantra during the portion of the night.

Indeed, by reciting ten thousand times with a spirit of devotion at the beginning of night on a Tuesday, one becomes liberated while living; or even by reciting a thousand or ten thousand times [on such occasions].
One should recite the Cintāmaṇi mantra on the surface of the earth; of this there is no doubt.
By the grace of the Cintāmaṇi, what on this earth is not accomplished? (73)
Having performed the ritual according to the prescribed rules at the abode of Manmatha, he who proceeds with a spirit of devotion shall go to the supreme goal. || 74 ||
A great lotus situated in the sky, perfectly worshipped by all the gods;
in its center resides Mahādeva, the blue-throated Sadāśiva. (75)
O Goddess, it is endowed with power, enchanting with all-encompassing bliss, white, red, blue-colored, and adorned with yellow and other hues. (76)
O Goddess, the God who is the supreme cause was meditated upon by the mind;
and meditation, O Goddess, was performed with the mind, and worship was offered with the mind. (77)
One should worship the Liṅga with the mind, perform libations and other rites with the mind, and likewise worship Kālikā, Tārā, and Bhujaṅginī with the mind.
"One should indeed establish the Brahma-nāḍī with the mind, which grants all desires;
thus, by means of the yoga of meditation, one should [worship] the Mother of the Universe with the mind. (79)
One should worship with supreme intelligence that auspicious Kālī, whose face is formidable, who dwells within the center of the Suṣumṇā; he shall certainly become the Lord of the Universe. 80.
One should bow down to the goddess Pārvatī, Mahānīlasarasvatī. I shall now describe the method of Ugratārā, which is difficult even for the gods to attain.
Within the lotus of the triangular enclosure, one should meditate day and night upon Mahānīla Sarasvatī, who is of the nature of Mercury. 82.
One should meditate upon Caṇḍī in the heart-lotus; one should meditate upon Śiva in the heart-lotus.
Having attained the state within the heart-lotus, O woman of excellent complexion, one should perform worship.
As long as there is the state of manifoldness, so long is there such diversity; therefore, actions are considered to be diverse according to their distinct natures. (84)
At that time, the gods—Brahmā, Viṣṇu, and Maheśvara—as well as Gaṇeśa, the Sun, Agni, and Varuṇa, were all divided. || 85 ||
And even Kubera, the guardian of the quarter—all these [deities] individually possess various activities consisting of female, male, and neuter natures. (86)
O Goddess of gods, the split bilva leaf is inferior to the tulasī leaf;
likewise, on this earth, the javā, droṇa, kṛṣṇā, and karavīra flowers are [inferior]. (87)
O Goddess of gods, it is indeed true that [all things] are distinct from the leaf of the tulasī;
for as long as one possesses a divine body, for that long one remains in the state of a bound soul (paśu). 88.
As long as there is the notion of duality regarding the Tantra, so long will there be separate ritual actions;
O Mother of the World, the notion of duality arises between Hari and Hara. (89)
Karālavadanā, Kālī, Śrīmadekajaṭā, Śivā, Ṣoḍaśī, Bhairavī, Bhinnā, and Bhuvaneśvarī—each distinct [from the others]. (90)
Chinnā, Bhinnā, and Annapūrṇā; Bhinnā and Bagalāmukhī; Mātaṅgī, Kamalā, and Bhinnā; and Vāṇī and Rādhikā. (91)
Their movements are diverse, their actions are diverse, and the collection of their speech and conduct is diverse, as long as unity does not arise in the lotus feet of Bhavānī. (92)
In non-duality, within the supremely purifying lotus feet of Tāriṇī,
which have arisen on the further shore of knowledge, [the state] likewise resides in the abode of the heart-lotus.
O lady of beautiful limbs, everything becomes one, consisting of the nature of Brahman;
[this occurs] among living beings, O Śāṅkarī. 94.
There is neither evil nor merit, neither Yama nor hell;
there is neither pleasure nor pain, and likewise no fear of diseases. (95)
There is neither fear nor sorrow; everything has Brahman as its essence.
[This applies to] the Brāhmaṇī, the Kṣatriyā, the Vaiśyā, the one born of a Vaiśya, the one born of a Śūdra, and even the outcaste woman. 96.
Just as the Vidyā is Tāriṇī, so too is the Vidyā;
such is knowledge, O Maheśānī, exactly as it arises, O beloved. (97)
In that very way, O Goddess of gods, Vidyā arises as the adversary of avidyā;
of this there is no doubt, and one becomes filled with the bliss of Brahman. 98.
And being endowed with supreme bliss, he will certainly attain liberation—non-duality, beyond the qualities, devoid of attributes, and transcending primordial nature (prakṛti). || 99 ||
Thus it is true, again it is true, and it is true, O fierce one of beautiful countenance:
there is nothing superior to the knowledge of reality, and there is no god higher than Sadāśiva. (100)
There is no state superior to the middle state, and there is no station equal to the difficult-to-attain one;
"I am he, I am he, again I am he, I am he"—thus indeed it arises. 101.
After a long time, that very knowledge arises within me;
indeed, having formed a sattvic perception of manifoldness as being essentially the Supreme Self.
And having grasped it, O lady of excellent hips, one becomes a knower of the ultimate truth;
there is nothing higher than knowledge, there is nothing, there is nothing, O fair-faced one. (103)
For having attained the supreme reality, one is liberated from the bondage of the body;
on the day of Kula, the noble one, observing the Kula-dharma and the Kula-vow, [is liberated]. 104.
One should resort to supreme bliss and indeed to supreme bliss alone;
there is no higher intellect than the noble family, nor any higher goal than the noble family.
"There is no higher devotion toward one of noble birth, nor is there any higher ritual act toward one of noble birth"—he who speaks thus indeed does not attain liberation. (106)
Right here, O Goddess of gods, is heaven; right here is the temple of Kailāsa.
Right here indeed are worldly enjoyment, devotion, and unfailing liberation.
O Consort of Śaṅkara, O Mistress of Tripura, O Caṇḍī, for the followers of Śakti, worldly enjoyment, heaven, and liberation are truly within the palm of their hand; of this there is no doubt. (108)
Śrī Pārvatī said:
O Nīlakaṇṭha, Mahādeva, Maheśvara, Teacher of the World!
O Lord, Master of the Universe, I ask about the supreme reality; please speak, O Protector. (109)
