How does liberation arise, and how is there enjoyment and devotion toward Maheśvara? O Śaṅkara, in what form does the individual soul attain the state of Śiva? (110)
Śrī Śiva said:
O Viśveśvarī, O Mother of the World, O Mahāmāyā, O Maheśvarī!
O Daughter of the Mountain, listen to these words, which are more secret than the most secret. (111)
O Maheśānī, one should take refuge in such a secret [teacher] with a spirit of devotion—one who is peaceful, self-controlled, of noble birth, and proficient in the meaning of all scriptures. (112)
Then, having first obtained a Guru who is the supreme cause,
one should receive the supreme mantra of the Goddess, O lady of excellent complexion.

Having understood the bridge (setu), the raft (kullukā), as well as the secret convention of mantras (mantrasaṅketaka), one should thoroughly practice the secret convention of the conduct of the pledge (samayācārasaṅketa) and the state of gnosis (jñānabhāva). || 114 ||
One should worship Pārvatī with supreme devotion according to the sequence of the chapters;
one should worship the Supreme Deity in accordance with the prescribed rules for the Guru.
She has four arms, ten arms, or is endowed with a thousand arms;
she has a flickering tongue, a terrifying mouth, and is adorned with a garland of severed heads.
One should bow down, recite prayers, meditate upon the Goddess, and worship her with offerings such as the beautiful *japā*, *aparājitā*, *droṇa*, and *karavīra* flowers. (117)
One should worship with red flowers that are fragrant, beautiful, and splendid;
O Goddess of gods, one should worship with various kinds of flowers with a spirit of devotion. 118.
With water for the feet, the respectful offering, and water for sipping, along with various other charming substances, with perfumes, flowers, incense, lamps, garments, and ornaments. || 119 ||
One should worship the Mother of the World with various kinds of food offerings, substances, and betel leaves for chewing that are rich in flavor, followed again by water for sipping.
O fair-faced one, worship should be performed in this manner according to one's ability;
having worshipped, one should then prostrate before Pārvatī with hymns composed from the tantras.

By the recitation of this hymn and even its armor-mantra (kavaca), Caṇḍī—the Mother of the Universe, the bestower of enjoyment and liberation, the giver of devotion, and the source of all auspiciousness—[grants her grace]. 122.
The external worship should be performed according to the instructions of the Guru; O Maheśvarī, the internal worship consisting of the inner sacrifice is the true external worship. 123.
All forms of worship should be performed until knowledge is born,
whether by bowing to Brahmins, by recitation, or even by austerity.
Māheśī became pleased by that hymn and by the armor-mantra (kavaca).
Then, O Goddess Maheśānī, when the Siddhividya is attained— || 125 ||
At that very moment, perfection is attained through worship and through action joined with wisdom;
thus, indeed, knowledge arises by the grace of the Goddess.
Then, O Caṇḍī, when the time has passed, both ritual action and devotion become fruitless;
liberation alone will be the beloved of Mahādeva.
Śrī Pārvatī said: I have indeed heard this supreme tantra, the essence of essences, higher than the highest;
by hearing which one attains liberation through the severing of the bonds of karma.
Śrī Śiva said:
Listen, O Goddess of beautiful hips, to my certain conclusion for you:
Durgā is indeed the supreme mantra; Durgā is indeed the supreme recitation.
Durgā is indeed the supreme sacred ford; Durgā is indeed the supreme ritual act;
Durgā is indeed the supreme enjoyment; and Durgā is liberation upon this earth.
Intellect, sleep, hunger, shadow, power, thirst, as well as forbearance, and action—whether Vedic or Tantric—which is most excellent among all. (131)
Thus, everything is indeed difficult to traverse; that which is not distinct from the Difficult-to-Traverse (Durgā) is not her recitation.
One should worship the pair of Durgā’s feet and remember Durgā day and night. (132)
O Goddess, one who, established in such devotion, performs the rite for Śivā, should mutter the supreme causal mantra "Durgā. (133)
Having become endowed with all accomplishments, one should dwell upon the circle of the earth;
O Daughter of the Mountain, various distinct practices have been taught by me in the various tantras. (134)
O Goddess, when there is the knowledge of oneness, then one shall attain perfection;
when one becomes equal-minded toward both the stationary and the moving.
O Pārvatī, Sovereign of the Universe, what is not accomplished for one both in this world and the next?
Thus, O Mother of the World, there is enjoyment, liberation, and devotion.
At that very end, your knowledge [will arise], and from that you shall attain nirvāṇa.
Thus it has been told, O Caṇḍī; what more do you wish to hear?
Śrī Pārvatī said:
"The supreme reality has indeed been heard; it has been heard with the highest reverence.
The life-story of Kālī has been heard by me, and the story of Tārā has also been heard."
Now I wish to hear how the accomplishment of mantra occurs, and how the accomplishment of vidyā occurs, O Lord; tell me that, O Treasure of Compassion. (139)
The illustrious Śiva said:
Now listen, O Goddess of gods, to the cause of the perfection of mantra—
the meaning of mantra and the consciousness of mantra— which was taught by me in the Yāmala.
O Caṇḍī, I shall speak in brief of the cause for the attainment of mantra-siddhi as it has been heard in the Ḍāmara, the Kuloḍḍīśa, and the Kulārṇava. (141)
O Great Goddess, what is the use of much speaking? One succeeds through devotion to the Guru. O Great Goddess, on a Kulavāra day, one should recite [the mantra] a thousand or ten thousand times.
On the fourteenth day or the new moon day of the month of Śanaiścara, or on a Tuesday,
the wise practitioner, intent upon the perfection of mantra, should sit upon a seat of kusha grass.
O fair-faced one, by reciting it ten thousand or a thousand times with a spirit of devotion,
and having then performed the internal sacrifice (antaryāga), one shall become a master of all supernatural powers (siddhis).
Whether at the foot of an Aśvattha tree, a Vaṭa tree, or the roots of a Nimba or Bilva tree, one should worship with supreme intelligence; thus a person shall attain the perfection of mantra.
O Sovereign of the Universe, O Great Illusion, O Destroyer of all obstacles!
One should perform this for three months; through this internal sacrifice, one becomes purified. (146)
Then one attains perfection; this is the truth, the truth, there is no doubt.
[One attains it by meditating on] the Goddess who dwells within the Suṣumnā, residing in the filaments of the lotus.
One should meditate with purified channels for unsurpassed success in mantra;
or else, O lady of beautiful limbs, hear my doctrine which is devoid of ritual action. (148)
By relying solely on meditation, the accomplishment of the mantra will certainly be attained;
one should meditate upon Kālikā, the supreme deity, within the lotus of the heart. 149.
Having established oneself in the perfection of yoga, the perfection of mantra comes to human beings;
that which was previously asked about and declared to be difficult to obtain on the surface of the earth.
That inquiry has been declared by you; what on earth would not be accomplished [therein], in the Śaktiyāmala, the Siddheśvara-tantra, and the Kulācala? (151)
The accomplishment of these vidyās is declared to be difficult to attain on the surface of the earth:
Kālī, Tārā, Mahāvidyā, and Bhuvaneśvarī, the sixteenth. (152)
Bhairavī, Chinnamastā, and likewise the Vidyā Dhūmāvatī;
Bagalā, the Siddhividyā, and Mātaṅgī whose nature is Kamalā. || 153 ||
These ten Mahāvidyās are proclaimed as the sciences of accomplishment;
this science has been declared in all the Tantras and kept secret. (154)
The eternal Śivā, who bestows all accomplishments and consists of eternal bliss—O Maheśānī, when the accomplishment of Vidyā occurs, it shall come to pass. 155.
O moon-faced one, you are the essence of the Moon; O fair-faced one, you are the state of Kubera; O consort of the Universe, you are the state of Śiva or the state of Viṣṇu. (156)
At that very moment, O Goddess of the gods, he becomes [so]; there is no doubt in this matter.
This is the section concerning the accomplishment of the Vidyā, as previously described, O Mistress of Tripura. (157)
Now I shall describe here the unsurpassed accomplishment of the vidyā, [to be practiced] in a cremation ground, at the root of an aśvattha tree, near a corpse, or in an empty temple. (158)
One should recite the Kālikā Tārā mantra; the Great Vidyā becomes propitious through recitation, austerity, hymns of praise, and captivating internal sacrifices. (159)
O Goddess, through worship and armor-mantras, the Great Vidyā becomes pleased;
indeed, for him who performs the worship according to this very procedure—ah! (160)
The world-sustainer Mahāmāyā, being perfectly propitiated, grants success;
she is the Great Vidyā who is the foremost cause for the attainment of mantra-perfection.
O Mother of the World, I have told you this; what more do you wish to hear?
Śrī Pārvatī said: I have heard the supreme cause of success which brings about all accomplishments;
by knowing which, the most wise living being attains liberation. (162)
O God of gods, O Lord of the universe, O Sovereign, I have heard various tantras;
now, O Nīlakaṇṭha, O Sadāśiva, I desire to hear [more]. (163)
O Lord of the gods, O Protector, since you are the husband of Kālikā, I desire to hear the majesty of both Kālikā and Tārā.
O Lord of Devas, you are the Moon; O Sadāśiva, speak quickly!
The illustrious Śiva said:
"O blessed one, you are devoted to your husband; O lady of beautiful limbs, listen to my words regarding the greatness of Kālikā and Tārā, which bestows spiritual perfection."
Just as Kālī is, so too is Tārā; indeed, their difference exists only at one time, according to the essential sequence of being the right-hand portion and the left-hand portion.
There is no worship equal to Kālī; there is no fruit equal to Kālī;
there is no knowledge equal to Kālī; and there is no austerity equal to Kālī. || 167 ||
Blessed is his mother, blessed is his grandfather, and blessed is his lineage and fame, O Caṇḍī, by whom Kālī has been duly worshipped. (168)
Kālī is equal to Tārā in the practice of vidyā, in the consideration of praise, in yantras, and in mantras; the fruit is identical, and there is no distinction whatsoever.
Thus, O beloved, has this conduct been described according to the perception of difference;
but, O Goddess of gods, when viewed with the perception of non-difference, all are equal, without a doubt. (170)
The glorious goddess Ekajaṭā, Ugratārā, and Sarasvatī [were present] for the subduing of serpents and for the protection of Kṛṣṇa in the waters of the Yamunā. || 171 ||
The liberating Vidyā Sarasvatī, blue in color, descended;
she was indeed [praised] by the gods, the lords of the gods, the lords of yogins, and the best of practitioners. 172.
By all the practitioners, sages, gandharvas, kinnaras, birds, vidyādharas, dancers, and also by various hosts of ṛṣis; 173.
Mahākālī and Mahānīlasarasvatī have been propitiated;
all practitioners declare that Kālī is the destroyer of time (death). || 174 ||
The Nīla-sarasvatī-vidyā, Ugratārā, and Manoharā;
and the majesty of Kālikā and Tārā, which is difficult even for the gods to attain. (175)
Who within the world is capable of knowing the greatness of that Goddess of the Suras, who consists of the ten and eighteen branches of knowledge? (176)
O Sovereign of the Gods, the best of practitioners who worships in this manner becomes exactly so;
O Goddess of Devas, hear thus this majesty which is difficult to find on earth. (177)
By the mere realization of which one becomes liberated while living;
as is Śiva, so is the individual soul (jīva), for the individual soul is indeed Śiva himself. (178)
Supreme knowledge arises from the knowledge of the inner state, O fair-faced one;
hear now another [instruction], O lady of beautiful limbs, and attend to it with care. (179)
O Maheśvarī, O Caṇḍī, I have not heard the hymn and the armor-mantra of the goddess Kālikā, nor that of Tārā, which cause the enchantment of all. (180)

O beloved, this mantra, which bestows success in the six rites, this hymn, and this supreme armor must not be revealed anywhere; it grants all prosperity. Now I shall speak here of the means for enchanting the living soul.
Śrī Pārvatī said:
Speak, O Lord, Sovereign of the World, Master Śrīkaṇṭha Śaṅkara!
[Tell me] the enchanting armor (kavaca), O Lord, as well as the hymn and indeed the armor itself. (182)
O Goddess, [tell me of that] which removes all obstacles and likewise brings about all peace;
O Lord, Teacher of the World, speak of that which is difficult even for the gods to understand. (183)
The illustrious Śaṅkara said:
Salutations to you, O beloved of the Lord of the Universe, O consort of Hara! O Sovereign of the Universe, O Sustainer of the World, perform the enchantment of the three worlds. (184)
O Goddess of the Suras, listen attentively as I shall proclaim the extraction of the mantra (mantroddhāra).

One should utter the remainder of the mantra-sacrifice joined with the Śakti;
O Mother of the World, whoever thus recites this King of Mantras—187.
Having become the Enchanter of the Three Worlds, he shall obtain all prosperity;
[the mantra is] the pair *dhā-ra*, the pair *phā-nta*, and the pair *tā-nta*, each followed by two dots (bindus). 188.
O Phakī, by means of this speech-empowering mantra, "Bring such-and-such a person under my control," one should recite it ten thousand times, or a thousand, or ten thousand times at night.
At that very moment, one may bring a goddess, a god, or a man under one's control;
this is the knowledge that brings others under control, hidden within all tantras. (190)
One should worship with a spirit of devotion and bow down to the one who deludes even kings;

O Goddess, if one recites this hymn on a Saturday during the night, in a very short time he shall become a favorite of the king. || 192 ||
O you with terrible fangs and a formidable mouth, O you who are fond of offerings of fish and meat!
Salutations to you, Mother of the Universe; salutations to you, the source of all existence.

Salutations to you, the bestower of supreme bliss, the enchantress of kings! 194.
Salutations to you, O eternal bliss; salutations to you, beloved of Śaṅkara;
salutations to you, Maṅgalā, the auspiciousness of all that is auspicious. || 195 ||
O Mother of the Universe, Sustainer of the World, salutations to you, O Sovereign of Tripura!
Salutations to you, O immeasurable Brahmā; salutations to you, O Śivā, the bestower of boons.
O Mother of the World, dark as a cloud, formidable, awe-inspiring, and auspicious; O Consort of Hara, worshipped by Hara, salutations to you who are adored by Hara! 197.
O you who are well-worshipped by the lord of monkeys, Brahmā, the moon, and others, and who possess the face of a lion;
homage be to you, O most fierce one, O most terrible one, O great festival! 198.
O Mahānandā, O Mahākālī, you who are worshipped by Mahākāla; O Sovereign of the Universe, salutations be to you; salutations to you, O Mistress of the World. || 199 ||
O Goddess who resides in Kāmarūpa, who fulfills desires, who is adorned with the flowers of desire, who bestows all desires, and who is praised in the temple of Kāma! || 200 ||

Obeisance to you, Caṇḍikā, the fierce one, the destroyer of Caṇḍa and Muṇḍa, who delights in the path of action, who desires the ultimate goal, and whose nature is the arts.

O Pārvatī, O Caṇḍī, you who are both as formidable as the sky rent asunder and yet terrifying;

Victory to you, O Goddess, Mother of the World! Victory to you, O Beloved of Hara!
Salutations to you, the bestower of bliss upon Śaṅkara, the beloved of Śaṅkara! 205.
Salutations to Kṛṣṇā, who is yellow in color and whose nature is both white and red;
to Mahānīlā, the blue-hued one, and to Mahānīla-Sarasvatī.
"O Vāgīśvarī, salutations to you; O Padmā, dweller in the lotus!
Thus, O Goddess, has this hymn that enchants all people been told to you. (207)

O Goddess, by the recitation of this hymn, one becomes a master of the world;

by hearing and reciting this armor (kavaca), one shall attain the perfection of the corpse (śavasiddhi). || 212 ||
May Pārvatī protect the head; may Jagadambikā protect the skull;
and may Maheśvarī Durgā protect both the skull and the cheek.

may Jagaddhātrī, the beloved of the bliss of the world, protect the region of the navel. 214.
May Caṇḍikā protect the heart; may the Supreme Deity protect the arms;
may the fifth Vidyā protect the hair; and may Bhairavī protect [me] in the assembly.
May Nityānanda protect my fame; may Liṅgeśvarī joyfully protect my phallus;
may Bhavānī protect my son, and may the daughter of Dakṣa protect my wife.
May Kāmākhyā, who dwells in the sky, eternally protect my entire body;
may the auspicious Mahākuṇḍalinī eternally protect my stomach.

may the goddess Durgā protect [me] in the forest, in the desolate place, in battle, and in the woods. (218)
"May the Goddess, the Mother of the World and Sovereign of the Three Realms, protect me in the water.
O Goddess, this armor (kavaca) is thus difficult to comprehend, O Enchantress of Kings. (219)
By reciting even the armor [mantra], one becomes a lord of the kings of kings.
O lady of excellent complexion, on whatever day this hymn and armor [mantra] are recited, [the result is attained]. (220)
By reciting this, one obtains all good fortune; there is no doubt about this.

O lady of excellent complexion, that which you asked has been explained in detail.
Now, O Goddess of the gods, what more do you wish to hear?

I know the heart of men, its hardness and its fickle mind;

In what form is she, Durgā, well-pleased upon the surface of the earth? By what hymn, by what armor (kavaca), or even by what knowledge does the Sovereign of the Universe—the Great Wisdom (Mahāvidyā)—become gracious toward the Supreme Cause? || 11 ||

by what form she is Kālī, Tārā, and Tripurasundarī. (12)
Bhairavī, Kamalā, Durgā, and Bhuvaneśvarī—
whatever Vidyās have been described, O Maheśānī, they are all called Bhuvaneśvarī.
That knowledge became manifest through pure gnosis alone;
for without gnosis, there is indeed neither meditation, nor ritual action, nor the attainment of the supreme state. || 14 ||
There is neither enjoyment nor liberation; indeed, there is no enjoyment, for it is only consciousness.
There is neither the accomplishment at the cremation ground nor the accomplishment consisting of a corpse.
O Maheśānī, neither consciousness nor spiritual accomplishment arises;
yet when knowledge has fully emerged, all accomplishments are perfected.
O Great Goddess, O Beloved, in every instance of knowledge, worship, recitation, austerity, devotion, ritual action, hymn of praise, and armor-mantra—all become fruitless if performed with doubt. 17.
Therefore, the supreme reality is knowledge, the ultimate means;
he who knows this, O Mother of the World, is Śiva—of this there is no doubt. (18)
O Goddess, one should never, under any circumstances, abandon that which pertains to the Kula;
O lady of excellent hips, if it is abandoned, everything becomes fruitless.
Thus, by means of the empowerment of Śakti, through the investigation of all things, one becomes liberated while living (jīvanmukta) in all the worlds; of this there is no doubt. || 20 ||
O Goddess of gods, O lady of excellent complexion, he who does not know the meaning of the mantra, the consciousness of the mantra, and the yonimudrā, knows nothing at all; this is the truth.
The convention, the convention of the gurus, and likewise the convention of the individual souls—of the divine ones, the heroes, and the bound souls (paśus), O woman of excellent complexion. (22)
O Goddess, [this is] the convention of existence, as well as the convention of Brahman;
it is the convention of the conduct of the pledge (samaya), the supreme practice of the hero (vīrasādhana). || 23 ||

thus have various methods been taught by me in the Yāmala, O beloved. (24)
Then he who is truly skilled in the Tantra attains perfection;
this has been declared in the Ḍāmara, O Dear One, as well as liberation in the Yamalaka.
O Maheśānī, O lady of excellent complexion, it has been stated in various tantras that by the mere service of Durgā, in accordance with the injunctions of the ritual texts, [one attains success].
A person attains liberation upon obtaining the truth that is captivating to the mind;
without the thorough knowledge of reality, there is neither happiness nor the supreme goal. (27)
O Goddess of gods, O Mother of the Universe, a person attains truth;
[she is] Kālī, with a terrifying face, adorned with a garland of severed heads. (28)
Kāmākhyā, Kāminī, Kāmyā, Karālāsyā, Digambarā, Aṭṭahāsā, Ghoranādā, Meghaśyāmā, and Bhayānakā. || 29 ||
She is the nature of all seeds, she whose form is the Great Seed;
she is the five-and-a-half-syllable Vidyā, worshipped by Vasiṣṭha and others.
She is served by the lords of the Siddhas, the lords of the Yogins, and even the lords of the Munis; she is worshipped by the lords of the gods, the lords of heroes, and the lords of practitioners.
Such is Mahāmāyā, the revealer of all reality;
I have heard the secret convention of both Kālikā and Tārā.
O beloved, the life-story of Bhairavī has been heard in the Kālītantra, the Bhairavatantra, and the Yāmalatantra,
but it has not been heard in the Bhairavītantra.

now, O fair-faced one, I shall relate it to you in brief.
Padmā, Triśakti, Dhanadā, Vāṇī, Pūrṇā, Maheśvarī, Durgā, Bhagavatī, and Devī—these are established as the protectors of the world. (35)
The sovereign of practitioners should worship that one Goddess, the sustainer of the world, who assumes various forms and is honored by the Omniscient One and others. (36)
Mahāmāyā, the sustainer of the world, adorned with every ornament;
she is Vāṇī, Māyā, and again Māyā, whose very nature is the Great Mantra.
And therefore, even by practitioners, that pure Māyā is resorted to—the three-syllabled Vidyā beginning with *pāśa*, which crushes the fear of Yama. (38)
She bestows all prosperity, she grants liberation, and she is beloved by liberation;
she is the knowledge consisting of the Great Yoga, and therefore she consists of all-knowledge. (39)
Worshipped by all practitioners, adorned with every ornament—thus, O Goddess, have they been described to you as those worshipped by the gods of gods. (40)
The Bhuvaneśī Mahāvidyā is difficult to obtain even for the gods;
O Goddess, if by the power of fortune a man obtains the fourth [day], he becomes composed of the four aims of life and attains the Supreme Brahman. || 41 ||
The Goddess said:

O God of gods, O Mahādeva, salutations to you, O Sadāśiva!

O Lord of the Universe, kinsman of the world, Sovereign of the world, Sadāśiva!
Homage be to you, O Mahādeva, Lord of the three worlds, Maheśvara!
Homage to you, knower of Yoga and Tantra; homage to the Lord of Kālī; homage! 47.
Salutations to you, O Lord of Tārā; salutations to you, O Lord of Bhairavī;

O giver of fruit, you who are the seed and the fruit of the tree of your own form;
salutations to you, the knower of all seeds; salutations be to you, the receptacle of the seed.
O Lord of Umā, salutations to you; salutations to you, O Three-eyed One!
O Five-faced One, salutations to you; salutations to you, O Moon-crested One! (50)
O Śambhu, Maheśvara, Vibhu, Virūpākṣa, Caturbhuja! Salutations to you, O Lord of the Mountain; salutations to the Lord of Caṇḍī. || 51 ||
O Lord of the three worlds, ocean of compassion, Śaṅkara who is the embodiment of mercy; O Lord of gods, beloved of your devotees, Nīlakaṇṭha, Sadāśiva!
Salutations to you, O Lord of Kāśī; salutations to you, O Moon-crested One. Salutations to you, O Lord of Caṇḍī; salutations to you, O Lord of Śrī, O Lord of Pārvatī.
Salutations to you, O support of the universe, O affectionate one with four faces;
salutations to you, O Lord of ritual action; salutations to you, O Lord who bestows liberation. (54)
"I am but a weak and young girl; how could I know, O Śaṅkara? Being devoid of qualities myself, I am in no way capable of knowing You who possess all qualities. (55)
Śrī Śiva said:
The attributeless Prakṛti is real, and I alone am likewise attributeless;
yet you are indeed always possessed of attributes, as I, Sadāśiva, am always possessed of attributes.
The Goddess is truly devoid of attributes; truly, truly, she is indeed without qualities.
Yet, for the sake of the accomplishment of her worshippers, she is considered to possess attributes, and [the Lord] is likewise considered to possess attributes.
O Goddess, the doctrines of various tantras have been revealed through various efforts;
who on this earth is capable of knowing the true nature of Brahman? (58)
Beasts of little intelligence run about in various directions;
having abandoned the lotus feet of Śrī Durgā, they go to the netherworld. 59.
I speak the truth; I speak firmly; I speak what is beneficial and wholesome again and again:
there is no liberation, indeed no liberation, without the service of Durgā. (50)

O Goddess, you have heard that Durgā is the Supreme Brahman; you have heard that Kālī is [the Supreme Brahman]; O Goddess, you have heard [it] regarding Tārā, and it has been heard by the best of Brahmans.
O Goddess, Brahmā, Viṣṇu, Rudra, Vāmana, and the celestial dwellers— indeed, we have become the best of practitioners through service at his feet.
Neither the Lord of Gods, nor Gaṇapati, nor Brahmā, nor Hara, nor Hari [is superior]; O Goddess, Hari, Hara, and I—all are devoted to Your lotus feet.
O Great Goddess, by your grace this Brahmā performs the work of creation;
by your grace Hari is the protector and Hara is the destroyer upon the surface of the earth.
And Vāsava, the lord of the immortals—[those of such] forms are remembered;
all of them, O Goddess, shall become free from old age on the surface of the earth through your grace. (65)
Through contact with your lotus feet, even Śaṅkara, the God of gods, [is purified];
therefore, O Beloved of the Lord of the Universe, O you who are affectionate toward your devotees! 66.
Cast your glance, O Mahāmāyā; salutations to her, salutations again and again!
You are Kālī, you are Tārā, and you are Ṣoḍaśī, O lady of beautiful countenance.
O Goddess, you are Bhuvanā, Bālā, Chinnā, and Dhūmā, O Maheśvarī; you are the goddess Bagalā, Bhīmā, and Kamalā, O Maheśvarī.
You are Mātaṅgī, you are Annapūrṇā, you are Dhanadā, O beloved of Śiva;
you are Durgā, the mother of the universe, possessing ten and eighteen forms.
She is the embodiment of the seven crores of great vidyās and the minor vidyās;
she is the maiden, beautiful in form, possessing a lovely appearance, and the daughter of the mountain king.

Worshipped by Śiva, adored by Śiva, worshipped by Brahmā, the Sovereign Goddess of the gods—Śiva is not distinct, nor is Śivā distinct; the beautiful-eyed one is not separate from the individual soul (jīva).
Thus I know, O Mistress of the Universe, this is the truth, the truth; there is no doubt. (71)
Śrī Pārvatī said:
"O Lord, you have spoken the truth to me; O Śaṅkara, you are the embodiment of truth. And I, O Śaṅkara, Lord of Pārvatī, am likewise known throughout the three worlds."
O Lord of the gods of gods, O omniscient one, tell me the distinction.
Śrī Śiva said:
"I do not know the specific details; tell them to me, O fair-faced one!
For you are omniscient, O Great Goddess, since you are the beloved of the Omniscient One. (73)
Śrī Pārvatī said: In Goloka I am Rādhā, and in Vaikuṇṭha I am the embodiment of Kamalā;
in Brahmaloka I am Sāvitrī, and in the form of speech I am Bhāratī.
On Kailāsa she was the goddess Pārvatī; in Mithilā, Jānakī;
in Dvārakā, Rukmiṇī; and in the city called Hastināpura, Draupadī.
I am Gāyatrī, the mother of the Vedas; I am Sandhyā for the twice-born;
I am Uṣā even in the midst of Yoga; and I am the Aparājitā Kṛṣṇā among flowers.
I am the *mālūra* leaf upon the vessel, and the nature of the womb (*yonisvarūpiṇī*) upon the seat;
I am the knowledge (*vidyā*) whose essence is Hari and Hara, worshipped by Brahmā, Viṣṇu, and Śiva.
O Lord Śaṅkara, she is to be recognized by her special grace alone;
O Protector, wherever a devotee of Śakti stands or moves, [there she is present]. 78.
In that very regard, O Mahādeva, I have reached this firm and supreme conclusion:
he who abandons the path of Śakti and pursues another path [is lost]. (79)
"Abandoning the jewel held in his hand, he runs after the state of ashes.
Thus, O Mahādeva, Lord of the World, have I spoken.
There is nothing higher than this, there is nothing, there is nothing, O Sadāśiva! (80)
[Thus ends the seventh chapter in the Muṇḍamālā Tantra. || 7 ||
[Now begins the eighth chapter.
The Goddess said:
"Salutations to you, O Lord of Pārvatī, Lord of the Universe, who are full of compassion!"
O Lord, Sovereign of the Universe, I have heard that there is nothing higher than knowledge.

O Lord of the wretched, ocean of compassion, Sovereign of the universe, Master of the world! O best of gods, I now desire to hear the supreme cause, the secret of Kālikā and Tārā, which is to be kept hidden.
The illustrious Śiva said: O Maheśvarī, what secret shall I speak even with my five faces,
or even with thousands of millions of tongues and hundreds of millions of mouths?
Nevertheless, O Śāṅkarī, I am unable in any way to describe his greatness; do I not know her secret and that which is to be hidden? (4)
Only he himself would be capable of recounting his own life-story in this manner;
otherwise, O Goddess of Gods, he would not know how to do so at all.
O Mother of the World, you have heard the hundred names of Kālikā in various tantras; yet this secret must be kept hidden within this tantra.
Karālavadanā, Kālī, Kāminī, Kamalā, Kalā, Kriyāvatī, Koṭarākṣī, Kāmākhyā, and Kāmasundarī. || 7 ||
Kāpālā, Karālā, Kāśī, Kātyāyanī, Kuhū, Kaṅkālā, Kāladamanā, Karuṇā, and Kamalārcitā. || 8 ||
Kādambarī, Kalaharā, Kautukī, Kāraṇapriyā;
Kṛṣṇā, Kṛṣṇapriyā, Kṛṣṇapūjitā, and Kṛṣṇavallabhā. || 9 ||
Kṛṣṇāparājitā, Kṛṣṇapriyā, and Kṛṣṇarūpiṇī;
Kālikā, Kālarātri, Kulajā, and Kulapaṇḍitā. || 10 ||
She is fond of the family dharma, possessed of desires, adorned with actions performed for the sake of desire;
she is dear to her family, devoted to her family, and honored by those of noble birth. || 11 ||
She who knows the lineage, who is Kamalā, who is worthy of worship, adorned by the hosts of Kailāsa;
she who is Kaṭajā, Keśinī, Kāmā, the giver of desires, and the one skilled in desire. || 12 ||
Karālāsyā, Kandarpā, adorned with the form of a passionate woman; Kolambakā, devoted to the *kola* fruit, playful, and adorned with hair. ||13||

She is the beloved of Keśava, she who shines like the *kāśa* flower, she who dwells in Kāśmīra, she who is worshipped by Keśava; she is the Mistress of Desire, whose form is desire, and who is adorned with the power to grant all desires.
The destroyer of time, fond of tortoise-flesh, worshipped by the tortoise and others;
she who sports, the granter of boons, the prison, and she who is devoted to the performance of actions. || 15 ||
She dwells in the midst of Kaṭakeśvara; she is worshipped by the insects of the forest; she is fond of the forest; she delights in the forest; she is devoted to the activities of the forest.
Devoted to the worship of virgins, served by hosts of maidens, born of noble family, beloved, dear to the Kaulas, and one who frequents the Kula. || 17 ||
She is of noble birth, knower of the family dharma, and the crusher of fear for her lineage;
she is fond of the dharma of desire, is herself desirable, and is the very embodiment of obligatory rites.
She who takes the form of desire, who removes desire, who is worshipped in the temple of desire;
she whose very nature is the abode of desire, known as Time (Kālā), and adorned by Time. || 19 ||
She who delights in ritual action, Kālī, the golden one, the bestower of desires;
she whose garment is the *kola* flower, Kolā, Nikolā, and the destroyer of the *kola*.
Adorned with Kośikī, Ketakī, Kumbhī, Kuntalā, and others—listen thus, O lady of beautiful limbs, to this secret that is the source of all auspiciousness. (21)
Whoever recites this with supreme devotion becomes Śiva himself; there is no doubt about this.
By the grace of these hundred names, what on earth cannot be accomplished? (22)
O Goddess, by the recitation of this secret [text], Brahmā, Viṣṇu, Rudra, and the celestial dwellers headed by Vāsava— all became free from their afflictions.
O Sovereign of the Three Worlds, there is nothing more to be hidden than this truth;
O Great Illusion, it does not exist at all within the Tantras.
O Goddess, O Maheśvarī, even without ritual action and without devotion,
you whose face is both serene and terrible become pleased by the recitation of this hymn, O Digambarī.
I speak the truth, O Great Goddess; there is nothing higher than this, neither in Gokula, nor in Vaikuṇṭha, nor in the abode of Kailāsa.
Therefore, O Sustainer of the World, there is no knowledge, hymn, or armor superior to this in the three worlds; it never exists [elsewhere]. (27)
O Goddess of the Gods, one should recite this supreme secret hymn with a spirit of devotion during the day or even at night.
Through the grace of the hundred names, the accomplishment of the mantra arises for whoever recites it during the night on the fourteenth day of the lunar fortnight on a Tuesday. (29)
He is accomplished, a knower of all scriptures, well-born, and ever pure;
he is a knower of lineages, a knower of time, and a knower of dharma upon this earth. (30)
O Goddess of the gods, O most beautiful one, by reciting this secret [text], one obtains the fruit arising from ten million rounds of purificatory rites; this is the truth. (31)
O lady of excellent hips, what on this earth cannot be accomplished through the recitation of this hymn?
The eight siddhis, beginning with aṇimā, shall surely be attained; of this there is no doubt. (32)
O Maheśvarī, at night, beneath a bilva tree, at the foot of an aśvattha tree, or beneath an aparājitā plant, one should recite the Kālikā-stotra according to one's ability.
By reciting it one hundred times, the perfection of the mantra will certainly be attained;
O Goddess of the Gods, there is no other means for the accomplishment of this great mantra. (24)
Therefore, O Goddess, there is nothing superior to this within the circle of the universe.
O Sovereign of the Gods, various tantras have been heard by you from my mouth.
The Muṇḍamālā Mahātantra is the means for accomplishing the Great Mantra; through devotion [to it], one attains the Goddess Durgā, the destroyer of suffering and poverty. (36)
He who should remember, recite, and meditate upon it is liberated; of this there is no doubt. He who is devoted to the Tantra should be known as one liberated while living (jīvanmukta). || 37 ||

O Daughter of the Mountain, for that practitioner who possesses great wisdom and is a constant follower of Durgā, there is neither lack of devotion, nor lack of liberation; indeed, there is no absence of liberation.
O Mother of the World, without Durgā, life would be fruitless for one who, though devoted to the path of Śakti, runs toward another path. (39)
And those capable of speaking do not see its limit, O beautiful one;
for, apart from Durgā, the Mother of the World, they are deluded by the web of words and the scriptures. (40)
Others, deluded by the scriptures, worship in this manner;
yet others, O Maheśvarī, do so without the Tantra, without the Mantra, and without the Yantra.
And neither devotion nor liberation arises, O woman of excellent complexion, [without him], for the Guru who speaks the Tantra is Śiva himself, the direct bestower of knowledge. (42)
O Maheśānī, as is the Guru, so is the Parama-guru;
as is the Parāpara-guru, so is the Parameṣṭhi-guru.
And likewise, the knower of the tantra, the teacher who himself expounds the tantra, as well as the tantra and the expounder of the tantra—these [fools] revile the tantric practice. (44)
Those people who are fierce are intent on chewing the flesh and bones of others;
for this very reason, they never disparage one who knows the Tantras.
They never laugh, they never cause harm, and they never speak [harshly]. || 45 ||
Śrī Pārvatī said:
Listen, O God, who are worshipped by the world; hear my words, which are firmly resolved.
By your grace, O Lord of Gods, the *Kālīrahasyaka* has been heard.
Now I wish to hear; speak concerning Tārā at this moment.
The illustrious Śiva said:
"O Goddess of the lords of gods, O Durgā, destroyer of the suffering of those in distress, you are blessed!
O daughter of the mountain, by hearing and reciting this, one attains liberation. (47)
She is the Savior, the tremulous, the slender, the Star, the creeper of the boat;
she is the form of the bank, dark at the shore, with breasts that are thin and diminished. 48.
Tuvīrā, Taralā, Tīvrā, Nayanā, Nīlavāhinī, Ugratārā, Jayā, Caṇḍī, Śrīmadekajaṭā, and Śivā. || 49 ||
Taruṇā, Śāmbhavī, Chinnā, Bhagā, Bhadratāriṇī, Ugratārā, Jayā, Caṇḍī, Śrīmadekajaṭā, and Śivā. (49)
Tarūṇā, Śāmbhavī, Chinnā, Bhagā, Bhadratāriṇī, Ugrā, Ugraprabhā, Nīlā, Kṛṣṇā, and Nīlasarasvatī. || 50 ||
The second [form] is Śobhinī, Nityā, Navīnā, and Nityanūtanā;
she is Caṇḍikā, Vijayā, the Goddess to be worshipped, and Gaganavāhinī. || 51 ||
She who possesses the loud laugh, whose face is formidable, and who is worshipped by the four-faced one (Brahmā) and others;
she who possesses attributes and is to be propitiated through attributes, and who is worshipped by Hari, Indra, and the gods. || 52 ||
She who loves red, she with red eyes, she who is blood-red, she adorned with all ornaments;
she who loves children, she who delights in children, Durgā, the powerful, and the strong.
She who is fond of strength, who delights in strength, and who is worshipped by Balarāma;
she who is the Mistress of half-her hair, whose hair is adorned with the Lord of Keśava.
Padmamālā, Padmā, Kāmā, Girinandinī, Dakṣiṇā, Dakṣā, Dakṣajā, and she who delights in the right (Dakṣiṇe-ratā). || 55 ||
She who loves the *vajra*-flower, who loves the red [lotus], adorned with flowers; she who belongs to Maheśvara, beloved by Mahādeva, and adorned with five [ornaments]. (56)
Iḍā, Piṅgalā, and Suṣumnā, who is the form of the vital breath (prāṇa), as well as Gāndhārī as the fifth, are worshipped by the five-faced one and others. || 57 ||
Thus, O Goddess, this supreme secret concerning the Self has been told;
by hearing it, one attains liberation through the grace of the goddess Tārā. (58)
Whoever should recite this secret hymn of Tārā, having become a master of all supernatural powers (siddhis), shall wander upon the circle of the earth. (59)
For him alone shall the mantra be perfected; the unsurpassed perfection of the mantra occurs thus, O Mahāmāyā—this is the truth, the truth, there is no doubt.
Whoever, being self-controlled, recites this at night on a Monday or a Tuesday,
for him there shall be the attainment of mantra-siddhi, and he shall obtain the state of a Gaṇapati.
Whether with faith or even without faith, whoever should recite the *Tārārahasyaka*, he shall in a very short time become liberated while living and attain the state of Śiva. (62)
O Goddess, by reciting it a thousand times, one obtains the fruit of the preliminary rite (puraścaryā).
Thus, those who are constantly disciplined worship Her while meditating upon Her. 63.
O Great Goddess, they have achieved their purpose by being liberated from the bondage of death and worldly existence;
you have heard the secret of the goddess Tāriṇī Kālikā.
This is the essence, most secret, to be meditated upon by Śiva, and the bestower of auspiciousness.
Now, O lady of noble hips, what more do you wish to hear? 65.
[Thus ends the eighth chapter in the Muṇḍamālā Tantra, within the secrets of Kālī and Tārā. || 8 ||
[Now begins the ninth chapter:
Having heard the secret from the mouth of the Lord of Pārvatī, the Great Goddess Pārvatī spoke to Mahādeva, the Great Lord, the Sovereign. (1)
Śrī Pārvatī said:
O Lord of the three worlds, O Master of the universe, O God of gods, O Sadāśiva!
By your grace, O Mahādeva, I have heard the various types of tantras.
Now indeed, faith in the scripture of the Āgamas has arisen within me alone.
If the Blessed One is pleased, please tell me the means that leads to great exaltation. (3)
O Great God, I have heard various kinds of doctrines in many tantras;
I am fulfilled, I am fulfilled, I am fulfilled, O Śaṅkara! (4)
O Lord, when Śaṅkara is pleased, what fear can there be on the surface of the earth? Without the grace of Śiva, nothing is ever accomplished.
Now I wish to hear the secret concerning Bhuvanā.
The illustrious Śaṅkara said:
Listen, O Goddess, I shall proclaim that which is the supreme secret among secrets; by practicing this, O Supreme Sovereign, one shall attain the perfection of mantra (mantrasiddhi). 6.
The primordial Śrī Bhuvanā, auspicious and capable of liberating one from the bonds of worldly existence;
she is Nārāyaṇī, the sustainer of the universe, the auspicious Śivā, the sovereign of the universe, and the supreme.
Gāndhārī is the supreme lore that causes the delusion of the world;
she is the sovereign of the gods, the mother of the universe, and the enchantress of the entire world. || 8 ||
She is Bhuvaneśī, Mahāmāyā, Deveśī, and the beloved of Hara;
she is Karālā, of formidable form, and the embodiment of the Great Seed-syllable.
The Goddess Tripureśī, the sovereign of the three worlds, Durgā, the mistress of the three realms, is eternal, stainless, and the bringer of all auspiciousness.
Gaurī, beloved of Sadāśiva, who is beautiful with all auspiciousness;
she is the bestower of Śiva, the giver of all good fortune, and whose very essence is auspiciousness. || 11 ||
With terrible fangs and a formidable mouth, fond of offerings of honey and meat,
Caṇḍī is the remover of all suffering and the bringer of all auspiciousness.
Pārvatī, the goddess Tāriṇī, Bhīmā, the destroyer of fear; the mother of the three worlds, Tārā, the savior, whose patience is as enduring as a young tree. 13.
She bestows enjoyment and liberation; she is devotion, the eternal beloved of Śaṅkara;
Umā, Gaurī, the dear one, the virtuous wife, the beloved, and the beloved of Varuṇa.
Bhairavī, the bestower of bliss to Bhairava, whose very nature is Bhairava;
she who is worthy of worship by Brahmā, the consort of Brahmā (Brahmāṇī), and Rudrāṇī, worshipped by Rudra. || 15 ||
She is Rudreśvarī, whose form is that of Rudra; she is considered Tripuṭā and Tripurā;
she is Bhavānī, the bestower of the bliss of Bhava, and the consort of Bhava. 16.
Caṇḍī, the Goddess worshipped by the gods; Pracaṇḍā, the one of terrible roar;
Ghanashyāmā, the one possessing clouds; Mahāghananinādinī, who resounds like a great thundercloud. || 17 ||
Ghorajihvā, Lalajjihvā, Vaideśī, Naganandinī, Trailokyamohinī, Viśvamohinī, and Viśvarūpiṇī. || 18 ||
The Sixteenth [Vidyā], Tripurā, the bestower of Brahman, the giver of Brahman, the sinless one—this is the supreme hymn of Brahman, the ultimate cause. (19)
He who recites this with supreme devotion is indeed liberated while living;
so too are all the deities beginning with Brahmā, and the sages who are experts in the Tantras.

Having recited it with supreme devotion, they shall attain the perfection of Brahman, provided they do not remain ignorant of the secret convention of the mantra as well as the secret convention of the vidyā. || 21 ||
O Goddess, the *vīrasaṅketaka* is a convention of great extent;
O Beloved, it consists essentially of the *yoni-mudrā*.
The convention of the observance of the pledge (samaya), as well as the family convention (kulasaṅketaka), the convention of Brahmā, O Caṇḍī, and likewise the convention of Kāla. || 23 ||
O Lord, O Master who deludes [the world], I have heard from the *Kulārṇava* the extensive explanations of the conventions of the *yantras* and the conventions of the *siddhis*. (24)
Śrī Śaṅkara said: The Mahāvidyā is proclaimed as the supreme among all sciences;
by the mere remembrance of which the perfection of mantras is produced. (25)
He who worships the Goddess who deludes the universe without knowing the secret convention of the mantras will not attain success, even by reciting them for a hundred years. (26)
The second is Vidyādyā, the sixteenth [form] Bhuvaneśvarī;
indeed, through the mere knowledge of Bhairavī, the Vidyās of accomplishment are attained. (27)
Between the iḍā and piṅgalā lies the Durgā, the deluder of the universe;
he who knows the method for piercing her is a wise man.
He is the blessed one, he is the successful one in this world, he is the hero, and he is pure in every respect;
he is to be known as Bhairava, who always increases happiness. (29)
He who knows her thus—the sustainer of the world, with a formidable face and adorned with a garland of severed heads—is indeed liberated while living. (30)
And I shall declare the distinction: one attains success through devotion to the *kula*.
O Goddess, without devotion to the *kula*, there is neither true devotion nor the attainment of the supreme goal. (31)
In the Kṛta age, Sundarī is the first; in Tretā, Bhuvaneśvarī;
in Dvāpara, the Vidyā Tāriṇī; and in the Kali age, Kālī is proclaimed.
O fair-faced one, I shall declare the difference in names and the difference in their cosmic cycles;
yet, O Mother of the World, there is no difference between Kālikā and Tārā.
O Tripureśvarī, [this is the mantra] of Ṣoḍaśī, Bhuvanā, Bhairavī, Chinnā, Dhūmā, and Bhīmā, O Supreme Goddess. (34)
Therefore, O Sovereign of the Gods, O Maheśānī, O lady of excellent complexion, there is no difference between the Vidyā of Bagalāmukhī and that of Mātaṅgī.
Śrī Pārvatī said:
O Viśvanātha, Mahādeva, Maheśvara, Teacher of the World!
O illustrious one, Lord of Yoga, whose banner is the bull, I ask you one thing. (36)
O Sadāśiva, O Śaṅkara, tell me the greatness of the *kṛṣṇā*, the *karavīra*, the *droṇa*, the *bilva* leaf, and the *japā*. (37)
Śrī Śiva said:
"O Śāṅkarī, you are blessed; you are devoted to your husband; you are as dear to me as my own life.
O Mother of the World, this is a most secret matter, exceedingly difficult even for the gods to obtain."
Kṛṣṇā is Aparājitā herself, Bhadrakālī without a doubt;
Karavīra is Bhuvanā, and Droṇa is Tripurasundarī. (39)
The Japā flower is the Goddess herself, the embodiment of all vidyās;
those practitioners who worship her, the beloved of Śiva, the Mother of the World, [attain success]. (40)
With these flowers, you shall worship Caṇḍī as Śivā; of this there is no doubt.
What need is there for recitations, or for austerities, or for gifts, or for offerings of the three sweets? 41.
By whom the Mother of the World was worshipped through recitations and other rites, as well as by means of the Rājasūya, Aśvamedha, Vājapeya, and Agnihotra sacrifices. || 42 ||
O Caṇḍī, whatever fruit arises from the worship of flowers—all that comes from the japā, the droṇa, the kṛṣṇa, the mandāra, and the karavīra; || 43 ||
One should present the actual form of Brahman to Mahādevī,
anointed with red sandalwood and joined with white sandalwood.
He who gives with a spirit of devotion is undoubtedly the Lord of the Universe,
even in the midst of great terror, a great portent, a great calamity, or a dire crisis.
In great suffering, in great disease, in great sorrow, and in great fear,
one should worship Kālikā, Tārā, Bhuvanā, Ṣoḍaśī, and Śivā.
Bālā, Chinnā, Bagalā, Dhūmā, Bhīmā, Karālinī, Kamalā, Annapūrṇā, Durgā, and Duḥkhavināśinī. || 47 ||

Having worshipped Kṛṣṇa upon the ground with all types of mantras, with recitations, and with beautiful Droṇa and Karavīra flowers, as well as with Mālūra leaves and black offerings, [one attains success].
O Maheśānī, that person shall become a supreme adept; of this there is no doubt.
[This is achieved] through the gift of hundreds of thousands of buffaloes, rams, goats, and auspicious donkeys.
If this mother of the world has been worshipped with offerings of flowers,
then Kṛṣṇā alone on this earth knows the true majesty of Kṛṣṇā.
Half of that, O Goddess, belongs to me; half of that always belongs to the Lord of Śrī (Viṣṇu);
half of that indeed belongs to the Lotus-born (Brahmā), and half of that belongs to the one who accomplishes the Vedas (Śiva). || 51 ||
O Daughter of Śaṅkara, I shall briefly describe the majesty of this flower:
on earth, in the netherworld, in heaven, in Vaikuṇṭha, and in the city of Kālikā.
O Mother of the World, I do not know what various fruits one might obtain through recitations, offerings of karavīra flowers, and acts of charity; who knows this except for Pārvatī? (53)
He who worships upon the surface of the earth with white and red oleanders mixed with red sandalwood will certainly become the Lord of the Universe.
Whoever worships the Goddess with *kṛṣṇāparājitā* flowers shall obtain the fruit of thousands of horse-sacrifices and become as auspicious as Śiva himself.
The greatness of the bilva leaf is difficult to attain even for the gods;
he who offers a bilva leaf to Śivā and to Śaṅkara [attains it]. (56)
Having become equal to Sadāśiva, he shall go to the abode of Brahmā;
even in the face of great calamity, O Goddess of Gods, one should perform the recitation of the Kṛṣṇāparājitā mantra.
He should go to Droṇa, Karavīra, or Kālikāpura;
for what is the use of foot-washing water, musical instruments, food offerings, or acts of worship? (58)
What is the use of offerings of honey, of madhuparka, or of kumbhaka, recaka, pūraka, or indeed of meditations and breath-restraints? || 59 ||
What is the use of recitations or austerities? What is the use of fish, meat, and the fifth [liquor]?
What is the use of other mantras, what of tantras, what of yantras, and what of ritual means (sādhana)? || 60 ||
Moreover, what indeed is the use of the Vasus, or of cremation grounds and the practice of mantras?
What is the use of sacrifices purified by mantras, or of the meanings of mantras, or of those who live by mantras? (61)
What is the use of the *yoni-mudrā*, or of sacred fords (*tīrtha*), or of the practices for attaining Brahman?
What is the use of the groups of *mātṛkā-nyāsa* mantras, or of *kaccha* grass, or of ritual jars and cloths? (62)

What is the use of the sixfold ritual placements (ṣoḍhānyāsa) like the beaks of crows, or of the means for accomplishing rites, if the Blessed Lady has been worshipped with oleanders (karavīra) and through recitations (japa) and other such practices? 63.
With *kṛṣṇāparājitā* flowers, charming *karavīra* blossoms,
*droṇa* flowers, *ketakī* flowers, and *japā* and *mālūra* leaves.
"For those by whom the Blessed Lady has been worshipped, what need is there for the accomplishment of ritual acts?
Thus, O Goddess, has this supreme and auspicious secret been heard.
Having heard this, the practitioner attains liberation; there is no doubt about this.
O Maheśānī, O beloved, this King of Tantras is the most essential of the essential.
Having heard and understood this, one quickly attains liberation; there is no doubt in this matter, even in the face of great fear, imprisonment, calamity, or many perils.
Having worshipped the Mother of the World, one is released from the bondage of worldly existence;
whoever worships Tāriṇī, whether with faith or without faith.
He is blessed, he is a wise poet, and he is an expert in the meaning of all scriptures;
he is honorable and he is a man of knowledge—he who worships Kālikā.
Thus has it been heard, O Goddess; what more do you wish to hear? (69)
[Thus ends the ninth chapter in the glorious Muṇḍamālā Tantra. 9.
[Then the tenth chapter:
The Śrī Devī said:
O God of gods, Mahādeva, Nīlakaṇṭha, Sadāśiva!
Salutations to you, O Supreme Lord; salutations be to you, O Lord of the Universe. || 1 ||
Salutations to you, O Supreme Lord, Sadāśiva, Maheśvara!
Salutations to you, O Supreme Bliss, the bestower of knowledge and liberation. || 2 ||
Salutations to you, O Lord of Pārvatī; salutations to you, O lover of your devotees.
Be gracious to me, O Kinsman of the World; tell me that which is to be kept secret, O Sadāśiva. (3)
Śrī Śiva said:
Listen, O Goddess, Mother of the World, to this supreme essence of essences;
by hearing it, the foremost of practitioners attains liberation upon the surface of the earth.
O Śivā, whoever should hear this Muṇḍamālā Tantra, the supreme cause, which bestows knowledge, liberation, and the bliss of devotion and emancipation; (5)
Thus, he who knows this supreme Goddess, who is difficult even for the gods to attain,
in the midst of the earth— he alone is the knower of the ultimate truth.
Without the path of Śakti, a living being possesses neither devotion nor a true state of existence;
the entire universe has its root in Śakti, and supreme austerity has its root in Śakti.
Supreme action, birth, and happiness on the surface of the earth have their root in Śakti;
O beloved, without the grace of Śakti, liberation does not arise.
"O Goddess of beautiful hips, you have heard everything that is to be kept secret on the surface of the earth.
What other secret remains? Tell me all of it, O lady of virtuous vows. (9)
Śrī Pārvatī said:
Listen, O God, Mahādeva; speak, O Teacher of the World!
Tell me, O Treasure of Compassion, how knowledge arises. (10)
Śrī Śiva said:
O Sovereign of the Gods, oh what fortune! Oh what fortune! Oh what fortune!
I have achieved my life's purpose, I have achieved my life's purpose, I have attained my kingdom, O Great Goddess!
O Great Goddess, the section on knowledge (jñānakāṇḍa) is auspicious, the most essential of the essential;
and that knowledge is to be known as twofold, difficult to be known even by the minds.
Knowledge called the supreme reality is the knowledge that accomplishes the object to be known;
other knowledge, which has delusion as its object, is considered common.
And thus, the remaining threefold [knowledge] is middling and devoid of reality;
O lady of noble limbs, the knowledge of reality is difficult for even the lords of yogis to attain.
Without the thorough knowledge of reality, worship and austerity are fruitless.
There is but one God, and I am one with Him, for there is no difference between my self and His body. 15.
O Maheśānī, from a pot, from a cloth, from Kālacakra, or from a tree—
when knowledge consisting of reality arises in this way, one is then liberated without delay.
The worship and meditation upon her are indeed manifold, as are the service of sacred fords and taking refuge at the feet of Tāriṇī. (17)
The remembrance of Saharāja, wandering through the lineage of the family, serving the company of the virtuous, and the worship of Viṣṇu as well as Śaṅkara. (18)
The worship of the pair of Kālikā’s feet is the cause of knowledge;
as long as you remain thus in mind, so long shall we remain distinct upon the surface of the earth.
For that long indeed do caste and lineage persist, for that long do various names endure, and for that long do all genders remain distinct; for the castes are indeed separate. (20)
To that extent are there friends and enemies; to that extent are there wives and kinsmen;
and to that extent are there various methods involving rituals, machines, mantras, and worship. (21)
For that long merit [endures], and for that long alone do merit and sin increase;
for that long you, this one, and she are born, O beloved. (22)

O fierce goddess, as long as that knowledge which opposes ignorance has not arisen—that knowledge which destroys ignorance and crushes both knowledge and ignorance—[so long does bondage persist]. (23)
That great lore which is the savior, the lore that transforms ignorance;
therefore, O lady of excellent hips, having produced this lore upon the earth— || 24 ||
O most beautiful one, it is true that one attains the liberation of Nirvana through unswerving devotion to the lotus feet of Śrī Durācaraṇa. (25)
At that very moment, the knowledge of Brahman—which is difficult even for Brahmā and others to attain—is born.
[It is through this that] Brahmā, Viṣṇu, Rudra, Vāsava, and the other inhabitants of heaven [attain their status]. (26)
The Bhairavas and Gandharvas are likewise eager for the practice of this lore;
the knowledge equal to the Knowledge of Brahman is this lore, and the ritual action equal to the Knowledge of Brahman is this ritual action. (27)
"There is no knowledge equal to the knowledge of Brahman; it never exists otherwise.
O Goddess, you have heard this knowledge of reality; what more do you wish to hear? (28)
Śrī Pārvatī said:
Salutations to you, O Mahādeva, Lord of the Universe, Teacher of the World!
O Mahādeva, I have heard various Tantras from your mouth.
Now, O Lord, speak the secret hymn of Caṇḍikā;
O Master, tell me the armor (kavaca), which is the cause of the awakening of the mantra.

O Maheśvarī, this [teaching] brings about the perfection of mantras, is more secret than the secret, and bestows liberation; by hearing it one attains liberation, and by knowing it, one attains the Vidyā.
Śrī Śiva said:
The path of Tāriṇī is difficult to attain; the state of Tāriṇī is difficult to attain;
the meaning of the mantra and the consciousness of the mantra are difficult to attain; and the practice with a corpse (śavasādhana) is difficult to attain.
The accomplishment through the cremation ground, the accomplishment through the womb, the accomplishment through Brahman;
the accomplishment through ritual action, the accomplishment through devotion, and the accomplishment through liberation. || 33 ||
O Goddess of gods, through the grace of this hymn, all supernatural powers (siddhis) are accomplished.
Salutations to you, O Caṇḍikā, O fierce one, O destroyer of Caṇḍa and Muṇḍa! || 34 ||
Salutations to you, O Kālikā, destroyer of the great fear of Time;
O Śivā, protect the world, O Mother of the Universe; be gracious, O beloved of Hara. (35)
I bow to the Sustainer of the world, who performs the protection of the world, the Vidyā who causes agitation in the world, and who ordains the creation of the world. || 36 ||
I bow to her who is formidable, awe-inspiring, and terrible; adorned with a garland of severed heads; worshipped by Hara, worthy of being propitiated by Hara, and the beloved of Hara.
I bow to Gaurī, beloved of the Guru, fair-complexioned and adorned with ornaments; the beloved of Hari, the Great Illusion (Mahāmāyā), who is worshipped by Brahmā. || 38 ||
She is the perfected one, the Mistress of the Perfected, accompanied by hosts of perfected Vidyādharas;
she bestows the perfection of mantra and the perfection of the womb, and is adorned with the *liṅga*.
I bow to Mahāmāyā, to Durgā, the destroyer of misfortune;
to Umā, who is of fierce nature, the fierce one, Tārā, accompanied by her formidable hosts.
I bow to Nīlasundarī, who is blue, dark as a blue rain-cloud, and beautiful in her azure hue;
she whose limbs are dark, who is fashioned from the color black, and who is adorned with a dark complexion. 41.
I bow to Gaurī, the sustainer of the world, who accomplishes all aims;
the sovereign of the universe, the formidable one, the fierce, who utters a terrible roar.
I salute the primordial Śrī Durgā, the first of the first Guru, worshipped by the first Lord, the bestower of wealth, Annapūrṇā, Padmā, and Sureśvarī.
I bow to the Mother of the Universe, the beloved of the moon-crested Lord, the beautiful Tripura, the youthful maiden adorned with a multitude of garlands. 44.
She who is the messenger of Śiva, worshipped by Śiva, the eternal object of Śiva’s meditation, the beautiful one, the savior, adorned by all the hosts of Śiva’s attendants. || 45 ||
She is Nārāyaṇī, worthy of worship by Viṣṇu, the beloved of Brahmā, Viṣṇu, and Hara;
she bestows all perfections, is both eternal and non-eternal, and is devoid of qualities.
She who possesses attributes and is devoid of attributes, who is to be meditated upon and worshipped, the bestower of all perfections;
she who grants the attainment of knowledge—she is the Great Knowledge (Mahāvidyā), the Great Goddess (Maheśvarī). 47.
I bow to Maheśī, the devotee of Maheśa, who is worshipped with great offerings of water,
the sustainer of the world, and the crusher of the demon Śumbha.
[She who is] fond of blood, red in color, the crusher of red seeds;
the Bhairavī, the goddess of the world, with a flickering tongue, the sovereign of the gods. 49.
The auspicious Tripureśī, beloved of Viśvanātha, the sovereign of the universe, the auspicious Śivā, who possesses four, ten, or eighteen arms. || 50 ||
Aṭṭahāsā, who delights in loud laughter; Dhūmravināśinī;
Kamalā; Chinnabhālā; Mātaṅgī; and Surasundarī. (51)
[She worships] Ṣoḍaśī, Tripurā, Bhīmā, Dhūmā, and Bagalāmukhī—the bestower of all perfections and the purifier of all vidyās and mantras. || 52 ||
"I bow to Jagattārā, the essence for the attainment of mantra-siddhi.
Thus, O lady of excellent hips, this hymn is the supreme bringer of success. (53)
O Daughter of the Mountain, by reciting this one attains liberation; this is indeed the truth on a Tuesday, the fourteenth day, the new moon, or a Thursday. (54)
When Venus has entered the night [the asterism of Śravaṇā], one shall attain liberation by reciting this hymn;
indeed, O Daughter of Śaṅkara, through the recitation of this hymn, the perfection of the mantra shall be achieved within three fortnights.
On the fourteenth day, during the latter part of the night, or likewise on a Saturday or Tuesday,
one should recite the hymn at the beginning of the night and shall attain the perfection of the mantra.
Indeed, from the mere recitation of this hymn, one attains unsurpassed perfection in mantra;
O Caṇḍī, by the recitation of this praise, the serpent goddess remains ever awake.
Having thus heard this hymn, O Pārvatī, now listen to the armor (kavaca).
Sadāśiva is the seer (ṛṣi), O Goddess, and the Uṣṇik meter is declared [for it]. (58)
And this is the application, O Goddess of gods, for the sake of attaining success in mantra:
"May Pārvatī protect my head; may she who is beloved by the Five-faced One protect me. (59)
May Caṇḍī protect the hair and the face; may Bhāratī, who is fond of blood, protect the throat, the breast, the skull, and indeed the cheek. (60)
Kālī, Karālavadanā, Vicitrā, Svaraghaṭṭinī, Rakṣāmūla, Nābhimūla, Durgā, and Tripurasundarī. (61)
May Tārā protect the right hand, and may Sarvāṇī protect everything;
may Viśveśvarī protect the back, and may Maheśvarī protect the eye.
May Kālikā protect the heart-lotus; may Ugratārā protect that which is situated in the sky;
may Nārāyaṇī protect the secret place; and likewise may Meḍhreśvarī protect the penis.
May Jayā protect the pair of feet, and Sundarī protect the toes;
may Ṣaṭpadmavāsinī protect every lotus [of the body] continuously.
May Iḍā and Piṅgalā protect me, and may Suṣumnā protect me at all times;
may Dhaneśvarī protect my wealth, and may Annapūrṇā always grant me sustenance.
May the external goddess protect the external; may Caṇḍikā always protect me.
May Pārvatī protect my life-force, and may Mātaṅgī protect me at all times.
May Chinnā, Dhūmā, and Bhīmā protect me from fear on land, in water, and in the forest;
and may Kaumārī, Vārāhī, and Nārasiṃhī likewise grant me glory. (67)
May Bhadrakālī, who dwells in the cremation ground, protect [me] eternally;
may Sarvāṇī and Sarvamaṅgalā always protect [me] in the belly. 68.
May the Mother of the World, who dwells on Kailāsa, protect Jaya forever;
may Śivapriyā protect her son, and Parvatanandinī protect her daughter.
May Bagalā protect the three worlds; may Bhuvaneśvarī protect the universe;
and may Pārvatī, who dwells in all abodes, protect every limb forever.
May Cāmuṇḍā, the accomplisher of all aims, protect my pores;
may Mahāvidyā, the eternally enchanting one, protect my cosmic egg (the universe). 71.
May Liṅga protect Liṅgeśvarī; may Maheśvarī protect Mahāpīṭha;
and may Tripureśvarī indeed protect Gaurī at the region of my joints.
May Sureśvarī always protect [me]; may she protect me in the cremation ground and upon a corpse;
likewise in the retention, the exhalation, and the inhalation of breath, and in the temple of Kāma.
May Kāmākhyā, the sovereign goddess of the gods, protect the abode of desire;
may Durgā protect me, as well as Ḍākinī, Kākinī, and likewise Śākinī—may they truly protect me. (74)
May Hākinī protect, may Rākiṇī protect always;
may Jvālāmukhī always protect, and may she always protect the face in the center.
May Tāriṇī protect me in prosperity, and may Bhavānī protect me in worldly existence;
may Trailokyamohinī protect my entire body, and may she protect me in solitude.
In the royal court, in great slaughter, in battle, and in the peril of enemies, may she who is fierce and the deluder of Bhairava protect me, the practitioner. (77)
May Śrī Rājamohinī protect me at the royal gate during calamities;
may Bhairavī, the bestower of prosperity, and Bālā protect my strength. 78.
"May the consort of Śambhu protect me eternally; may Tripurāntakā protect me.
Thus, O Goddess, has this secret that is valid for all times been told. (79)
Bestowing enjoyment and liberation, providing happiness and granting all prosperity—he who, having risen at dawn, recites this shall become a sovereign among practitioners on earth. (80)

On a Thursday coinciding with the fourteenth lunar day, on a new moon day, or on a Saturday, that best of practitioners who, having worshipped the Guru on a Thursday, should recite [this], [attains success]. || 81 ||
He goes to the abode of the Goddess; this is the truth, the truth, there is no doubt—if one recites thus, O lady of excellent limbs, being devoted with supreme faith. (82)
He shall attain the perfection of mantras before long; of this there is no doubt.
Having obtained the fruit of a hundred thousand recitations of the *puraścaraṇa*, he should worship Śivā. 83.
Having reached the royal road, which is the auspicious path, the individual soul becomes Śiva;
by reciting the armor-verse (kavaca) and the hymn, one certainly attains liberation. 84.
Having recited the armor-verse (*kavaca*) and the hymn (*stotra*), the ascetic should worship the ten sciences (*daśavidyā*);
the perfection of the sciences and the perfection of the mantra will surely come to pass—of this there is no doubt. (85)
At that very moment, success regarding the betel-leaf arises; there is no doubt about this.
Success regarding a corpse and success regarding a funeral pyre are difficult to attain upon the surface of the earth.
Success is easily attained without effort through betel; of this there is no doubt—at the beginning of the night, during the night, at the great hour (mahākāla), and in the latter part of the night.
O Maheśānī, he who recites this with devotion shall indeed attain the status of a leader of the Gaṇas. || 87 ||
[Thus ends the tenth chapter, titled "The Mantra-Siddhi Stotra-Kavaca," in the Muṇḍamālā Tantra. 10.
[Thus ends the first section, the Muṇḍamālātantra.]
